AI.motivation: Existing MLLM-based video understanding methods rely on uniform sampling or frame selection, which optimize either broad temporal coverage or local relevance but fail to preserve both global storyline context and fine-grained evidence simultaneously due to token limitations.
AI.method: VideoRouter organizes each video into a question-agnostic temporal hierarchy of coarse-to-fine temporally coherent segments, generating two complementary views: a global view for coverage-oriented reasoning and a local view for detail-oriented evidence recovery. A verification-guided router then determines which view is better supported by the selected evidence and selects the final answer.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show the verification-guided router effectively coordinates global and local reasoning. On VideoMME, VideoRouter outperforms state-of-the-art frame selection methods by 2.9 points under the LLaVA-Video-7B backbone.
AI.conclusion: Coordinating complementary evidence views via a temporal hierarchy with verification-guided routing is a more effective paradigm for long-video understanding than selecting a single frame subset, and the code will be released.

title: Uncertainty-Aware World Model for Aerial Image-Goal Navigation
summary: Aerial image-goal navigation requires an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) to reach a target location specified by a goal image. Existing world-model-based methods rank candidate trajectories using predicted futures, but typically rely on only one or a few point predictions, which is inadequate for large-scale outdoor environments with substantial future-state uncertainty. To address this limitation, we propose the Uncertainty-Aware Navigation World Model (UA-NWM), an efficient latent world model for aerial image-goal navigation, which formulates trajectory scoring as conditional out-of-distribution detection. UA-NWM represents plausible futures with an uncertainty subspace and decomposes the prediction--goal discrepancy into uncertainty-explainable and unexplainable components. Only the unexplainable residual is used for scoring, enabling robust selection without multiple future samples. Extensive experiments demonstrate that UA-NWM consistently outperforms existing navigation world models while maintaining low inference latency. Real-world UAV experiments further validate its practical applicability. Project page: https://duryi.github.io/UA-NWM-Project-Page

AI.tldr: UA-NWM is an efficient latent world model for aerial image-goal navigation that formulates trajectory scoring as conditional out-of-distribution detection, decomposing prediction-goal discrepancy into uncertainty-explainable and unexplainable components, enabling robust trajectory selection without multiple future samples.
AI.motivation: Existing world-model-based navigation methods rely on only one or a few point predictions for trajectory ranking, which is inadequate for large-scale outdoor environments with substantial future-state uncertainty.
AI.method: UA-NWM represents plausible futures with an uncertainty subspace and decomposes the prediction-goal discrepancy into uncertainty-explainable and unexplainable components. Only the unexplainable residual is used for scoring, enabling robust selection without multiple future samples.
AI.result: UA-NWM consistently outperforms existing navigation world models while maintaining low inference latency. Real-world UAV experiments further validate its practical applicability.
AI.conclusion: The uncertainty-aware formulation effectively addresses future-state uncertainty in aerial navigation, achieving superior performance with practical real-world viability.

title: ALTER: Modeling Longitudinal Changes via Regional Differencing for 3D CT Report Generation
summary: Computed tomography (CT) is widely used for clinical diagnosis and longitudinal follow-up, yet automatically generating accurate and complete radiology reports from three-dimensional (3D) CT remains challenging. Existing methods improve fine-grained correspondence between images and text by modeling anatomical regions, but remain centered on the current examination. Consequently, patient-specific longitudinal changes within individual regions remain insufficiently modeled. Meanwhile, interval changes are often distributed across multiple anatomical regions, complicating a coherent assessment of the overall longitudinal state. We propose Anatomically Localized Temporal Evidence Representation (ALTER) to address these limitations. Global Prior Integration (GPI) incorporates the prior CT and report to establish historical context for the current examination. Regional Proxy Differencing (RPD) enables each current anatomical region to retrieve a historical proxy from a single shared encoding of the prior volume and to derive localized interval evidence. Interval Change Fusion (ICF) further combines current abnormality states with region-distributed differences, converting their joint representation into change-aware soft prompts that guide report generation. ALTER achieves state-of-the-art results on most evaluation metrics across the RadGenome-ChestCT validation and CTRG-Chest-548K test sets. Code and data preprocessing details are available at https://github.com/peytonkarlie/ALTER/tree/main.

AI.tldr: ALTER is a novel framework for 3D CT radiology report generation that incorporates historical CT scans and reports to model patient-specific longitudinal changes across anatomical regions, achieving state-of-the-art performance on two large benchmark datasets.
AI.motivation: Existing CT report generation methods model anatomical regions for image-text correspondence but remain focused on the current examination only, failing to capture patient-specific longitudinal changes. Since interval changes are often distributed across multiple regions, coherent assessment of overall longitudinal state is difficult, motivating the need for temporal evidence integration.
AI.method: ALTER consists of three components: (1) Global Prior Integration (GPI) incorporates the prior CT and report to establish historical context; (2) Regional Proxy Differencing (RPD) lets each current anatomical region retrieve a historical proxy from a shared encoding of the prior volume to derive localized interval evidence; (3) Interval Change Fusion (ICF) combines current abnormality states with region-distributed differences into change-aware soft prompts for report generation.
AI.result: ALTER achieves state-of-the-art results on most evaluation metrics across the RadGenome-ChestCT validation and CTRG-Chest-548K test sets.
AI.conclusion: Leveraging historical context and regional interval differencing enables more accurate and complete longitudinal radiology report generation from 3D CT, outperforming existing methods on multiple benchmarks.

title: TruthLens: Object Hallucination Detection via Self-Evaluating Truthfulness Scores in LVLMs
summary: Despite the remarkable progress of large vision language models (LVLMs), object hallucination remains a fundamental challenge that hinders their trustworthy deployment. A key finding motivates our work: real and hallucinated object tokens are clearly separable in hidden representations, yet this separability is largely lost at the language-modeling (LM) head. We propose TruthLens, a self-evaluation framework that teaches the LM head to expose a per-object truthfulness signal without any auxiliary model or additional inference cost. Concretely, a rarely-used special token is repurposed as a reference token. For each object-token position, we extract the log-probability assigned to this special token by the LM head, and define its difference from a predefined constant as the truthfulness score. The model is then fine-tuned with an MSE objective that drives scores toward 1 for real objects and 0 for hallucinated ones, while a divergence constraint preserves the original generation capability. Despite being trained on only a limited set of object categories, TruthLens generalizes effectively to benchmarks with substantially larger label spaces. Extensive experiments across multiple LVLMs demonstrate state-of-the-art performance; notably, on Qwen2.5-VL-7B, TruthLens outperforms the previous best method on MS-COCO by over 17\% in AUROC. Our code is available at https://github.com/wyqstan/TruthLens.

AI.tldr: TruthLens is a self-evaluation framework that teaches LVLMs to expose per-object truthfulness signals directly from the LM head, repurposing a rarely-used special token and fine-tuning with an MSE objective plus a divergence constraint, achieving state-of-the-art hallucination detection without auxiliary models or extra inference cost.
AI.motivation: Object hallucination remains a fundamental challenge hindering trustworthy deployment of large vision language models (LVLMs). A key observation drives the work: real and hallucinated object tokens are clearly separable in hidden representations, but this separability is largely lost at the language-modeling (LM) head, suggesting an untapped opportunity to recover and expose this signal.
AI.method: TruthLens repurposes a rarely-used special token as a reference token. For each object-token position, the log-probability assigned to this special token by the LM head is extracted, and its difference from a predefined constant defines the truthfulness score. The model is fine-tuned with an MSE objective pushing scores toward 1 for real objects and 0 for hallucinated ones, while a divergence constraint preserves original generation capability.
AI.result: TruthLens generalizes effectively from limited training object categories to benchmarks with substantially larger label spaces. Extensive experiments across multiple LVLMs demonstrate state-of-the-art performance; notably, on Qwen2.5-VL-7B it outperforms the previous best method on MS-COCO by over 17% in AUROC.
AI.conclusion: TruthLens provides an effective, lightweight, and training-efficient solution for object hallucination detection in LVLMs, with strong generalization and superior performance without auxiliary models or additional inference cost.

title: Dual-Output Multi-Exposure HDR Reconstruction via SDR Fusion and Gain Map Inverse Tone Mapping
summary: We propose DOME-HDR, a dual-output multi-exposure HDR reconstruction framework that jointly produces a perceptually balanced SDR image and a consistent HDR image via gain map inverse tone mapping. Given three bracketed LDR inputs, DOME-HDR first synthesizes a base SDR using a LoRA-adapted latent diffusion model. A dual cross-attention fusion module injects complementary structural and color cues from the under- and over-exposed images while anchoring on the mid exposure for stability. The synthesized SDR then guides HPGM, our HDR Prior-guided Gain Map network, to predict a spatially varying gain map for reliable dynamic-range expansion. We evaluate on Kalantari, Tel, and Challenge123 using both full-reference and no-reference metrics, where DOME-HDR achieves state-of-the-art HDR reconstruction quality; ablations further confirm the effectiveness of dual cross-attention and SDR-guided gain map estimation.

AI.tldr: DOME-HDR is a dual-output multi-exposure HDR reconstruction framework that jointly produces a perceptually balanced SDR image (via a LoRA-adapted latent diffusion model with dual cross-attention fusion) and a consistent HDR image (via an HDR Prior-guided Gain Map network that uses the synthesized SDR for dynamic-range expansion). It achieves state-of-the-art results on Kalantari, Tel, and Challenge123 datasets.
AI.motivation: Multi-exposure HDR reconstruction from bracketed LDR inputs remains challenging, and most existing methods focus solely on HDR output without jointly producing a perceptually balanced SDR counterpart. There is a need for a framework that can simultaneously deliver both a visually pleasing SDR display image and a high-quality HDR image.
AI.method: DOME-HDR consists of two main components: (1) a LoRA-adapted latent diffusion model that synthesizes a base SDR image from three bracketed LDR inputs, using a dual cross-attention fusion module to inject structural and color cues from under-/over-exposed images while anchoring on the mid exposure; (2) HPGM (HDR Prior-guided Gain Map network) that uses the synthesized SDR to predict a spatially varying gain map for reliable dynamic-range expansion to produce the HDR output.
AI.result: DOME-HDR achieves state-of-the-art HDR reconstruction quality on Kalantari, Tel, and Challenge123 datasets evaluated with both full-reference and no-reference metrics. Ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of the dual cross-attention module and SDR-guided gain map estimation.
AI.conclusion: The dual-output HDR/SDR framework with diffusion-based SDR synthesis and prior-guided gain map prediction provides a promising approach for high-quality multi-exposure HDR reconstruction, validated by SOTA performance and ablative evidence.

title: SCI-CLIP: Segment-Centric Inference with Reference Memory for Training-Free Open-Vocabulary Segmentation
summary: Training-free open-vocabulary segmentation remains limited by a missing inference abstraction. Frozen vision-language features are produced at patch level, yet dense prediction requires a unit that simultaneously governs feature interaction, spatial support, contextual recovery, and retrieval-based correction. We present SCI-CLIP, a segment-centric inference framework built around the principle that the same region abstraction should organize all stages of dense open-vocabulary prediction. SCI-CLIP first induces a region-consistent interaction graph over frozen visual tokens, then reconstructs dense features by propagating values over this graph, augmenting them with selective cross-window support only where local evidence is insufficient. The same segment abstraction is subsequently used to construct and query an offline reference memory, aligning exemplar retrieval with the units on which prediction is made. SCI-CLIP turns frozen CLIP-style features into spatially coherent, context-aware, and retrieval-compatible dense predictions without any training. SCI-CLIP consistently improves the structural quality of dense predictions, the robustness of contextual reasoning, and the alignment of exemplar-based correction, yielding stronger open-vocabulary segmentation across eight benchmarks. Project code is available at: https://github.com/mzamini92/SCICLIP.

AI.tldr: SCI-CLIP is a training-free inference framework for open-vocabulary segmentation that uses a consistent segment abstraction across all stages—feature interaction, spatial support, contextual recovery, and retrieval-based correction—turning frozen CLIP-style features into spatially coherent dense predictions without training, improving performance across eight benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Training-free open-vocabulary segmentation lacks a unified inference abstraction. Frozen vision-language features are produced at patch level, but dense prediction requires a unit that simultaneously governs feature interaction, spatial support, contextual recovery, and retrieval-based correction.
AI.method: SCI-CLIP first induces a region-consistent interaction graph over frozen visual tokens, then reconstructs dense features by propagating values over this graph and augmenting with selective cross-window support where local evidence is insufficient. The same segment abstraction is used to construct and query an offline reference memory for exemplar retrieval aligned with the prediction units.
AI.result: SCI-CLIP consistently improves structural quality of dense predictions, robustness of contextual reasoning, and alignment of exemplar-based correction, yielding stronger open-vocabulary segmentation across eight benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: A segment-centric inference framework (SCI-CLIP) demonstrates that unifying all stages around the same region abstraction enables training-free, spatially coherent, context-aware, and retrieval-compatible dense open-vocabulary prediction.

title: ChronoVision: Temporal Reasoning via Latent State Reconstruction
summary: Multimodal large language models excel at passive perception but struggle with complex visual cognitive tasks requiring multi-step temporal reasoning. This degradation largely stems from the inherent ambiguity of language-based reasoning, which often fails to accurately articulate continuous visual transformations. To address this, we propose ChronoVision, a multimodal framework designed to align visual logic with latent imagery. During supervised fine-tuning, a Reconstructive Visual Head predicts the latent representation of the final transformed state, while an ROI Attention Locating module focuses the model on key visual evidence via semantic span queries. In post-training, we apply reinforcement learning with an implicit process grounding mechanism, guided by a composite reward function that evaluates outcome correctness, latent process alignment, and unsupervised visual focus. Furthermore, we introduce Vbvr-VQA, a novel dataset that evaluates temporal tracking by reformulating video reasoning into a strict image-ordering task. Experiments demonstrate that ChronoVision achieves state-of-the-art performance on Vbvr-VQA with 74.8% in-domain and 71.6% out-of-domain accuracy, alongside a strong 55.0% accuracy on IntPhys2, a highly challenging cross-domain benchmark.

AI.tldr: ChronoVision is a multimodal framework that improves temporal visual reasoning in LLMs by aligning visual logic with latent imagery through a Reconstructive Visual Head during SFT, an ROI Attention Locating module, and reinforcement learning with implicit process grounding. It introduces the Vbvr-VQA dataset for image-ordering-based video reasoning and achieves 74.8% in-domain and 71.6% out-of-domain accuracy on Vbvr-VQA, plus 55.0% on IntPhys2.
AI.motivation: Multimodal LLMs struggle with complex visual cognitive tasks requiring multi-step temporal reasoning due to the inherent ambiguity of language-based reasoning, which fails to accurately articulate continuous visual transformations.
AI.method: ChronoVision aligns visual logic with latent imagery via three components: (1) a Reconstructive Visual Head that predicts latent representations of final transformed states during supervised fine-tuning; (2) an ROI Attention Locating module that focuses on key visual evidence via semantic span queries; (3) post-training with reinforcement learning using an implicit process grounding mechanism and a composite reward function evaluating outcome correctness, latent process alignment, and unsupervised visual focus. They also introduce Vbvr-VQA, a dataset reformulating video reasoning into a strict image-ordering task.
AI.result: ChronoVision achieves state-of-the-art 74.8% in-domain and 71.6% out-of-domain accuracy on Vbvr-VQA, and 55.0% accuracy on the highly challenging cross-domain IntPhys2 benchmark.
AI.conclusion: Latent imagery alignment and process grounding effectively overcome language ambiguity in temporal visual reasoning, yielding strong performance on both in-domain and cross-domain benchmarks.

title: Vorch-IR: Long-Form Unified Multimodal Identity Replacement Video Generation
summary: Video identity replacement seeks to transfer the identities of one or more subjects while preserving the motion, expressions, and temporal structure of a driving video. Existing methods largely target single-person settings and often require task-specific structural controls, such as masks or pose representations, limiting their flexibility in general multimodal editing systems. Progress on multi-person replacement is further constrained by the scarcity of paired training data. We present Vorch-IR, a unified framework that supports single- and dual-person identity replacement, with optional background replacement, in a single model. Built on LTX2, Vorch-IR jointly conditions on a driving video, indexed reference images, and a textual editing instruction. The reference images need not match the pose, layout, or spatial configuration of the driving video: their roles as subject or background references are specified through the instruction. Dense visual conditions are fused through self-attention, while a vision-language context establishes semantic correspondence through cross-attention. We further develop an automatic data construction pipeline that synthesizes paired supervision for all four editing settings. Experiments using automatic metrics and pairwise human evaluation demonstrate strong identity preservation, motion fidelity, and temporal coherence across diverse scenarios. A temporal overlapping inference strategy additionally extends the short-clip model to minute-long generation without autoregressive continuation.

AI.tldr: Vorch-IR is a unified framework built on LTX2 that supports single- and dual-person identity replacement (with optional background replacement) in a single model, conditioned on driving video, indexed reference images, and textual instructions, using self-attention for dense visual fusion and cross-attention for semantic correspondence, with an automatic data pipeline and temporal overlapping inference for extended generation.
AI.motivation: Existing video identity replacement methods are largely limited to single-person settings, require task-specific structural controls (e.g., masks or pose), and lack flexibility for multimodal editing. Multi-person replacement is further hindered by the scarcity of paired training data.
AI.method: Vorch-IR jointly conditions on a driving video, indexed reference images, and a textual editing instruction. Reference images are instruction-specified as subject or background references without requiring pose/layout matching. Dense visual conditions are fused via self-attention; vision-language semantic correspondence is handled through cross-attention. An automatic data construction pipeline synthesizes paired supervision for all four editing settings (single/dual person × with/without background replacement), and a temporal overlapping inference strategy extends short clips to minute-long generation without autoregressive continuation.
AI.result: Experiments using automatic metrics and pairwise human evaluation demonstrate strong identity preservation, motion fidelity, and temporal coherence across diverse scenarios, including minute-long generation.
AI.conclusion: Vorch-IR provides a unified, flexible framework for single- and dual-person identity replacement with optional background replacement, overcoming data scarcity via automatic data synthesis and enabling long-duration generation without autoregressive drift.

title: Vorch-Streamer: Extending Human Audio-Visual Generation to Real-Time Long-Form Streaming
summary: Real-time long-form avatar audio--video generation requires causal, continuous synthesis while maintaining audiovisual synchronization and visual consistency. Adapting a pretrained bidirectional model to this setting presents two key dilemmas. First, autoregressively reusing generated blocks as context creates exposure bias, causing errors and visual drift to accumulate over long rollouts. Second, a global speech utterance does not indicates a causal generator which portion should be spoken next when only limited local audio--video context is available. We present \textbf{Vorch-Streamer}, a post-training framework that addresses these challenges and enables real-time long-form Text-to-Audio-Video (T2AV) streaming. We construct a synthetic corpus of 80K avatar clips spanning 12--21 seconds and first train a causal generator with mixed Teacher Forcing and Diffusion Forcing. We then apply long-horizon Self Forcing with DMD distillation, exposing the model to its own rollout distribution while preserving the quality of the pretrained bidirectional teacher. To explicitly control speech progression, an external language model predicts discrete 25-Hz speech-planning tokens, whose continuous features condition the audio diffusion branch and align each causal block with the content it should speak. With bounded causal context and four-step denoising, Vorch-Streamer jointly generates audio and video from text at 27.12 FPS, exceeding the 24-FPS real-time playback rate while maintaining competitive audio--lip synchronization and strong identity preservation over long-form generation.

AI.tldr: Vorch-Streamer is a post-training framework that enables real-time long-form text-to-audio-video streaming by adapting a pretrained bidirectional model into a causal generator, using mixed Teacher Forcing and Diffusion Forcing, long-horizon Self Forcing with DMD distillation to reduce exposure bias, and external speech-planning tokens to control speech progression—achieving 27.12 FPS generation with competitive audio-lip sync and strong identity preservation.
AI.motivation: Real-time long-form avatar audio-video generation is challenging because adapting pretrained bidirectional models to causal streaming settings introduces two dilemmas: (1) autoregressive reuse of generated blocks creates exposure bias causing error accumulation and visual drift over long rollouts, and (2) global speech utterances do not indicate to a causal generator which portion should be spoken next with only limited local context available.
AI.method: The authors build a synthetic corpus of 80K avatar clips (12-21 seconds), train a causal generator with mixed Teacher Forcing and Diffusion Forcing, apply long-horizon Self Forcing with DMD distillation to expose the model to its own rollout distribution while preserving pretrained bidirectional teacher quality, and use an external language model to predict discrete 25-Hz speech-planning tokens whose continuous features condition the audio diffusion branch to align each causal block with its intended speech content.
AI.result: With bounded causal context and four-step denoising, Vorch-Streamer generates audio and video jointly from text at 27.12 FPS, exceeding the 24-FPS real-time playback rate while maintaining competitive audio-lip synchronization and strong identity preservation over long-form generation.
AI.conclusion: Vorch-Streamer successfully addresses the exposure bias and speech-progression control challenges for real-time long-form T2AV streaming, achieving real-time rates while maintaining quality in synchronization and identity persistence.

title: Dual-Attention and Adversarial Transfer Networks for Sim-to-Real Cross-Orientation Wireless Sensing
summary: Millimeter-wave human activity recognition suffers significant performance degradation when the user's orientation changes relative to the sensing system, yet collecting labeled multi-orientation data is labor-intensive and costly. To eliminate the need for exhaustive multi-orientation measured data, we develop a physics-guided simulator that synthesizes orientation-diverse wireless training data from single-orientation motion. Specifically, to suppress orientation-induced feature variations, we propose a dual-attention network that extracts activity-discriminative and orientation-robust representations from dual-link Doppler spectrograms. To bridge the simulation-to-reality gap, we introduce an adversarial unsupervised transfer learning mechanism that aligns feature distributions using only a small number of unlabeled target-domain samples. The S2M-Sense platform shows high fidelity in reproducing real-world signatures, validated against 60.48 GHz mmWave measured data with an average structural similarity index measure (SSIM) of 0.84 between simulated and measured Doppler spectrograms across all 4 activities and 4 orientations. Experimental results show that S2M-Sense achieves 88.33% recognition accuracy using only the dual-link multi-orientation simulated dataset, which improves to 95% after simulation-to-reality transfer learning with as few as 16 unlabeled measured samples. Both cases with and without transfer learning outperform state-of-the-art cross-domain sensing methods.

AI.tldr: S2M-Sense is a physics-guided simulator that synthesizes orientation-diverse mmWave training data from single-orientation motion, paired with a dual-attention network and adversarial unsupervised transfer learning to achieve 95% recognition accuracy across user orientations with as few as 16 unlabeled real samples.
AI.motivation: mmWave human activity recognition degrades significantly when user orientation changes, but collecting labeled multi-orientation data is labor-intensive and costly. The authors aim to eliminate the need for exhaustive multi-orientation measured data.
AI.method: (1) A physics-guided simulator generates orientation-diverse wireless training data from single-orientation motion. (2) A dual-attention network extracts activity-discriminative and orientation-robust features from dual-link Doppler spectrograms. (3) An adversarial unsupervised transfer learning mechanism bridges the simulation-to-reality gap using a small number of unlabeled target-domain samples.
AI.result: The simulator achieves high fidelity (SSIM of 0.84 vs measured data). S2M-Sense reaches 88.33% accuracy using only simulated multi-orientation data, improving to 95% after transfer learning with only 16 unlabeled measured samples. Both cases outperform state-of-the-art cross-domain sensing methods.
AI.conclusion: Physics-guided simulation combined with domain adaptation can effectively replace costly multi-orientation data collection, achieving competitive or superior performance while requiring minimal real-world unlabeled data.

title: URNet: A Unified Reparameterized Network for Efficient RGB-D Semantic Segmentation
summary: Previous RGB-D semantic segmentation methods commonly employ dual encoders to separately process RGB and depth inputs, followed by dedicated modules for cross-modal feature fusion. However, such designs often inadequately capture depth representations and consequently limit effective cross-modal interaction, while the additional encoder branch introduces redundant computation that hinders lightweight execution. To tackle these challenges, we propose URNet, a Unified Reparameterized RGB-D Network that performs simultaneous multi-modal feature extraction and cross-modal fusion within a single encoder. Specifically, we adopt a reparameterization strategy to compact the network architecture and facilitate fast inference. Within each Reparameterized Block (RepBlock), a Linear Gated Attention (LGA) module is introduced to fully exploit complementary RGB and depth cues across different feature scales. Furthermore, considering that decoder design has been relatively underexplored in existing RGB-D segmentation models, we develop a concise yet effective universal decoder, termed the Pyramid Merging Decoder (PMD). Extensive experiments on multiple RGB-D segmentation benchmarks demonstrate that URNet achieves state-of-the-art performance while maintaining high efficiency. Code will be available at https://github.com/Wild-Stephen/URNet.

AI.tldr: URNet is a unified reparameterized RGB-D semantic segmentation network that performs multi-modal feature extraction and cross-modal fusion within a single encoder, using Reparameterized Blocks with Linear Gated Attention and a Pyramid Merging Decoder, achieving state-of-the-art performance with high efficiency.
AI.motivation: Existing RGB-D segmentation methods use dual encoders with dedicated fusion modules, which inadequately capture depth representations, limit cross-modal interaction, and introduce redundant computation that hinders lightweight execution.
AI.method: URNet uses a single unified encoder with reparameterization for compact architecture and fast inference. Each Reparameterized Block (RepBlock) contains a Linear Gated Attention (LGA) module for exploiting complementary RGB and depth cues across feature scales. A Pyramid Merging Decoder (PMD) is proposed as a concise and effective universal decoder.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on multiple RGB-D segmentation benchmarks demonstrate that URNet achieves state-of-the-art performance while maintaining high efficiency.
AI.conclusion: URNet effectively addresses the limitations of dual-encoder designs by unifying feature extraction and fusion in a single encoder, delivering both high accuracy and efficiency for RGB-D semantic segmentation.

title: DistMedVL: Distributional Vision-Language Alignment for Uncertainty-Aware Medical Image Segmentation
summary: Cross-modal alignment of visual and textual representations is fundamental to multimodal medical image understanding, yet remains hindered by uncertainty in both modalities under real-world clinical conditions. Existing vision-language segmentation methods rely on deterministic cross-modal matching, which overlooks aleatoric uncertainty from ambiguous boundaries and epistemic uncertainty from limited training data, leading to fragile performance under domain shift. To address this issue, we propose DistMedVL, a probabilistic vision-language framework that introduces a lightweight Probabilistic Cross-Modal Adapter (PCM-Adapter) upon frozen encoders to explicitly model representational uncertainty. Specifically, the PCM-Adapter comprises two sequential modules for progressive probabilistic alignment. We first devise a Mahalanobis Alignment Module (MAM) that models textual tokens as Gaussian distributions and computes patch-text compatibility via Mahalanobis distance, yielding variance-conditioned matching that downweights unreliable feature dimensions. Moreover, we devise a Distribution Flow Module (DFM) that estimates modality-wise confidence parameters and performs vision-guided refinement of textual distributions, accommodating distributional variation across imaging modalities. Extensive experiments across eight medical segmentation benchmarks demonstrate that DistMedVL outperforms state-of-the-art methods with only 6.3M trainable parameters, exhibiting superior data efficiency, perturbation robustness and cross-dataset generalization.

AI.tldr: DistMedVL is a probabilistic vision-language framework for medical image segmentation that models cross-modal alignment as distributions rather than deterministic matches, using a lightweight PCM-Adapter with Mahalanobis alignment and distribution flow modules to capture aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty, achieving state-of-the-art performance across eight benchmarks with only 6.3M trainable parameters.
AI.motivation: Existing vision-language segmentation methods perform deterministic cross-modal matching, which fails to handle aleatoric uncertainty (e.g., ambiguous anatomical boundaries) and epistemic uncertainty (e.g., limited training data), resulting in fragile performance under real-world clinical conditions and domain shift.
AI.method: DistMedVL introduces a Probabilistic Cross-Modal Adapter (PCM-Adapter) built upon frozen encoders, comprising two sequential modules: (1) a Mahalanobis Alignment Module (MAM) that models textual tokens as Gaussian distributions and computes patch-text compatibility via Mahalanobis distance, performing variance-conditioned matching that downweights unreliable feature dimensions; and (2) a Distribution Flow Module (DFM) that estimates modality-wise confidence parameters and refines textual distributions with vision-guided updates to accommodate distributional variation across imaging modalities.
AI.result: Extensive experiments across eight medical segmentation benchmarks show DistMedVL outperforms state-of-the-art methods with only 6.3M trainable parameters, demonstrating superior data efficiency, perturbation robustness, and cross-dataset generalization.
AI.conclusion: Probabilistic cross-modal alignment that explicitly models uncertainty in both modalities provides a more robust and parameter-efficient alternative to deterministic matching for multimodal medical image segmentation, particularly under domain shift and limited data conditions.

title: SciQNet: Two-Stage Multimodal Adaptation for Scientific Image Quality Assessment
summary: Scientific images are essential for communicating experimental observations, quantitative evidence and conceptual knowledge. Unlike natural images, their quality depends on both visual clarity and scientific informativeness, making assessment challenging. In this work, we present SciQNet, a two-stage multimodal adaptation framework for scientific image quality assessment. The first stage performs domain-adaptive pretraining on scientific document images and the second stage conducts task-specific fine-tuning with joint scoring and understanding supervision. For scoring-oriented supervision, we combine instruction tuning with a Huber loss derived from rating-word logits, while understanding-oriented supervision is formulated as multiple-choice visual question answering. Experiments show that using a 40% stratified subset of the domain-adaptive data gives the best performance among the evaluated pretraining fractions, suggesting that pretraining-data relevance may be as important as pretraining-data scale. The final model achieves an SIQA-S score of 92.21, an SIQA-U score of 47.38 and a combined score of 69.80. This work presents our solution to the ICME 2026 Scientific Image Quality Assessment Challenge, which ranked 2nd in the scoring track.

AI.tldr: SciQNet is a two-stage multimodal adaptation framework for scientific image quality assessment, combining domain-adaptive pretraining with task-specific fine-tuning using joint scoring and understanding supervision. It achieved 2nd place in the ICME 2026 Scientific Image Quality Assessment Challenge scoring track.
AI.motivation: Scientific image quality assessment is challenging because quality depends on both visual clarity and scientific informativeness, unlike natural images where visual clarity alone is the primary criterion. Existing approaches do not adequately address this dual nature.
AI.method: SciQNet uses a two-stage framework: (1) domain-adaptive pretraining on scientific document images, and (2) task-specific fine-tuning with joint supervision. Scoring supervision combines instruction tuning with a Huber loss derived from rating-word logits, while understanding supervision is formulated as multiple-choice visual question answering.
AI.result: Using a 40% stratified subset of domain-adaptive data gives the best performance among evaluated pretraining fractions, achieving an SIQA-S score of 92.21, SIQA-U of 47.38, and combined score of 69.80. Ranked 2nd in the scoring track of the ICME 2026 challenge.
AI.conclusion: The paper demonstrates that pretraining-data relevance matters more than scale for this task, and that joint scoring-and-understanding supervision effectively improves scientific image quality assessment.

title: TAU-Bench: From Anomaly Instance Tracking to Fine-Grained Video Anomaly Understanding
summary: Humans understand anomalous events through a coherent perceptual process in which they identify the focal instance, follow its behavior as the event unfolds, and interpret why it violates the expectations of the surrounding scene. Video anomaly understanding (VAU) seeks to endow models with a similar capability, moving beyond deciding whether a video is anomalous toward explaining how the event develops and why it matters. Although recent vision--language models (VLMs) can generate detailed and plausible anomaly descriptions, their semantic fluency does not ensure that these interpretations remain grounded in the correct anomaly instance over time. Existing benchmarks typically evaluate tracking and semantic understanding through separate protocols, leaving such instance--semantic inconsistency largely unmeasured. We therefore introduce TAU-Bench, a track-centric benchmark for jointly evaluating anomaly instance tracking and fine-grained anomaly understanding. TAU-Bench contains 1,118 videos, 1,454 tracks, and 202,438 pixel-level masks spanning 49 event and 45 scene categories, together with track-centric annotations that connect instance-level identification, event-level understanding, and scene-level reasoning. To build TAU-Bench at scale, we developed an automated data engine integrating anomaly suitability filtering, anomaly instance track construction, hierarchical caption annotation, and human quality control. Evaluations across representative VLM families show that models producing plausible anomaly interpretations may still fail to localize and track the correct instance reliably, revealing a persistent gap between semantic reasoning and visual grounding. These findings therefore highlight instance-grounded evaluation as an important step toward more faithful and reliable VAU systems.

AI.tldr: TAU-Bench is a track-centric benchmark for jointly evaluating anomaly instance tracking and fine-grained video anomaly understanding, containing 1,118 videos, 1,454 tracks, and 202,438 pixel-level masks across 49 event and 45 scene categories. The benchmark reveals that VLMs producing plausible anomaly descriptions often fail to correctly localize and track the anomalous instance over time, exposing a gap between semantic reasoning and visual grounding.
AI.motivation: Existing video anomaly understanding benchmarks evaluate tracking and semantic understanding separately, leaving the instance-semantic inconsistency problem—where models generate fluent descriptions but fail to stay grounded in the correct anomaly instance over time—largely unmeasured. Humans understand anomalies through a coherent process of identifying the focal instance, following its behavior, and interpreting why it violates scene expectations, and VAU systems should mirror this capability.
AI.method: The authors introduce TAU-Bench, a track-centric benchmark that jointly evaluates anomaly instance tracking and fine-grained understanding. The benchmark includes 1,118 videos, 1,454 tracks, 202,438 pixel-level masks, and 49 event / 45 scene categories, with track-centric annotations connecting instance-level identification, event-level understanding, and scene-level reasoning. They built it using an automated data engine integrating anomaly suitability filtering, anomaly instance track construction, hierarchical caption annotation, and human quality control.
AI.result: Evaluations across representative VLM families show that models producing plausible anomaly interpretations may still fail to localize and track the correct instance reliably, revealing a persistent gap between semantic reasoning and visual grounding in current video-language models.
AI.conclusion: Instance-grounded evaluation is an important step toward more faithful and reliable video anomaly understanding systems. The findings highlight the need to bridge the gap between semantic fluency and visual grounding in VAU.

title: StreamArena: Toward Continuous, Interactive, and Long-Horizon Agentic Streaming Video Understanding
summary: Deploying autonomous multimodal agents in continuous, real-world environments requires them to ingest unbounded audio-visual streams and maintain hour-scale memory. However, current evaluations predominantly rely on brief clips and multiple-choice formats. This design allows minimal baselines that process only the last four frames to match or surpass complex streaming models, while answer options also expose language shortcuts. We introduce StreamArena, a benchmark for hour-scale, interactive streaming video understanding. StreamArena contains 243 full-length videos averaging 88.8 minutes and 3,646 rigorously annotated, open-ended question-answer pairs that evaluate real-time perception, historical retrospection, proactive interaction, and multimodal tool utilization. Evaluation across diverse systems exposes a tension between continuous interaction and long-horizon multimodal comprehension. Methods that retain only recent frames cannot recover distant events, methods that convert past observations into text lose visual evidence, and methods that repeatedly compress visual memory struggle to preserve fine-grained details over time. We address this tension with StreamMind, a two-tier architecture that assigns latency-critical interaction and proactive monitoring to independently scheduled frontend workers, while backend workers asynchronously construct persistent multimodal memory and perform historical recall and external search. StreamMind outperforms existing streaming baselines across all four capabilities and reduces query-to-answer latency by reusing persistent state.

AI.tldr: StreamArena is a benchmark for hour-scale interactive streaming video understanding with 243 full-length videos and 3,646 open-ended QA pairs. The paper also introduces StreamMind, a two-tier architecture that separates latency-critical frontend workers from backend workers handling persistent multimodal memory, which outperforms existing streaming baselines across four key capabilities.
AI.motivation: Current evaluations of autonomous multimodal agents rely on brief clips and multiple-choice formats, which allow minimal baselines (e.g., processing only last four frames) to match complex streaming models and expose language shortcuts. There is a need for benchmarks that evaluate hour-scale, interactive streaming understanding in continuous real-world environments.
AI.method: StreamArena benchmark: 243 full-length videos (avg 88.8 min) with 3,646 open-ended QA pairs evaluating real-time perception, historical retrospection, proactive interaction, and multimodal tool utilization. StreamMind architecture: two-tier system with independently scheduled frontend workers for latency-critical interaction/proactive monitoring, and backend workers asynchronously constructing persistent multimodal memory, handling historical recall and external search.
AI.result: StreamMind outperforms existing streaming baselines across all four capabilities and reduces query-to-answer latency by reusing persistent state. The evaluation reveals a tension between continuous interaction and long-horizon comprehension, exposing limitations of frame-only retention, text-based past conversion, and repeated visual compression approaches.
AI.conclusion: Long-horizon streaming video understanding requires architectures that balance real-time interaction with persistent multimodal memory, and the proposed two-tier StreamMind architecture demonstrates an effective solution to this tension.

title: G$^2$ARD-GS: Geometry-Guided Anchor-Regularized Gaussian Splatting Distillation
summary: Dense colored LiDAR maps provide accurate city-scale geometry, but lifting them into 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) retains millions of primitives, making the resulting models costly to store, transmit, render, and adapt. Aggressive primitive reduction alleviates this burden, but can remove the local surface support needed for stable novel-view synthesis and downstream geometric use. We introduce G$^2$ARD-GS, a geometry-guided distillation method that converts a dense Gaussian prior instantiated either as a training-free point-cloud lift or a trained GS model into a compact, reusable representation. G$^2$ARD-GS progressively consolidates the prior into surface-aware representatives, then recovers appearance on the resulting fixed topology under construction-time anchor constraints, with no primitives added or removed during recovery. Under limited supervision, geometry-aware view selection allocates the available view budget. On MatrixCity, G$^2$ARD-GS achieves the best PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS across matched $5\times$--$30\times$ compression budgets, outperforming PUP by $3.2$--$6.8$,dB in PSNR. When reused as frozen geometry, the compact model improves off-trajectory appearance adaptation by $3.7$--$4.9$,dB over PUP 3D-GS and preserves image-to-model registration accuracy on Cambridge KingsCollege at $30\times$ compression. Project page: https://patrick1159.github.io/gardGS-page/.

AI.tldr: G²ARD-GS is a geometry-guided distillation method that compresses dense colored LiDAR-based 3D Gaussian Splatting models into compact, surface-aware representations, achieving state-of-the-art compression (5x-30x) with improved rendering quality and downstream usability.
AI.motivation: Dense colored LiDAR maps lifted into 3DGS retain millions of primitives, making models costly to store, transmit, render, and adapt. Aggressive primitive reduction removes the local surface support needed for stable novel-view synthesis and downstream geometric tasks.
AI.method: G²ARD-GS progressively consolidates a dense Gaussian prior (either a training-free point-cloud lift or a trained GS model) into surface-aware representatives, then recovers appearance on the fixed topology under construction-time anchor constraints with no primitives added or removed. Under limited supervision, geometry-aware view selection allocates the available view budget.
AI.result: On MatrixCity, G²ARD-GS achieves the best PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS across matched 5x-30x compression budgets, outperforming PUP by 3.2-6.8 dB in PSNR. As frozen geometry, it improves off-trajectory appearance adaptation by 3.7-4.9 dB over PUP 3D-GS and preserves image-to-model registration accuracy on Cambridge KingsCollege at 30x compression.
AI.conclusion: G²ARD-GS demonstrates that geometry-guided distillation can produce compact 3DGS representations that retain geometric fidelity, enabling both high-quality rendering and downstream geometric applications under aggressive compression.

title: LAWM-3D: Learning 3D-Aware Latent Actions from Human Videos for Generalizable Robot World Models
summary: World models enable agents to perform forward rollout and planning without real-world interaction. However, their application in open-world embodied intelligence remains limited by the high cost of action annotations and the heterogeneity of action spaces across platforms. Recently, latent action models (LAMs) have alleviated this bottleneck by learning action representations directly from unlabeled human videos in a self-supervised manner. Nevertheless, most existing LAMs rely on single-view inputs and operate primarily in 2D pixel space, raising a fundamental question: can simply incorporating multi-view videos into LAM training endow the learned latent actions with 3D-aware perception? Our study shows that the answer is negative. The primary reasons lie in future-frame appearance leakage as well as inter-camera appearance discrepancies and viewpoint variations. To address these issues, we propose LAWM-3D, which introduces three tightly coupled key designs: (1) a multi-view invariant unified action tokenization scheme for learning 3D-aware latent actions; (2) a geometric alignment constraint that anchors intermediate encoder features to a pretrained 3D foundation model, thereby explicitly providing cross-view geometric correspondences; and (3) a non-injective RGB-D joint reconstruction objective that prevents shortcut learning from future-frame appearance information, forcing the LAM to focus supervision on motion cues with geometric significance. Importantly, these components are not simply stacked but are tightly coupled through a unified motivation. Built upon a two-stage paradigm of large-scale human video pretraining followed by robot fine-tuning, extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed 3D-aware latent actions significantly improve world model performance, achieving SOTA results in generation quality, physical consistency, and generalization ability.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes LAWM-3D, a framework that learns 3D-aware latent actions from multi-view unlabeled videos for world models in embodied intelligence. The authors show that simply adding multi-view videos to latent action model (LAM) training fails due to appearance leakage and viewpoint discrepancies, and introduce three tightly coupled designs: multi-view invariant action tokenization, geometric alignment with a 3D foundation model, and a non-injective RGB-D joint reconstruction objective. The method achieves SOTA performance in generation quality, physical consistency, and generalization.
AI.motivation: World models are limited in open-world embodied intelligence by the high cost of action annotations and heterogeneous action spaces. Latent action models (LAMs) learn from unlabeled videos but are predominantly single-view and 2D-pixel based. The paper investigates whether multi-view inputs can naturally endow LAMs with 3D awareness and finds the answer is negative, motivating the need for explicit 3D-aware designs.
AI.method: LAWM-3D introduces three tightly coupled components: (1) a multi-view invariant unified action tokenization scheme for learning 3D-aware latent actions; (2) a geometric alignment constraint anchoring encoder features to a pretrained 3D foundation model to provide cross-view geometric correspondences; and (3) a non-injective RGB-D joint reconstruction objective that prevents shortcut learning from future-frame appearance leakage. These are built on a two-stage paradigm of large-scale human video pretraining followed by robot fine-tuning.
AI.result: Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed 3D-aware latent actions significantly improve world model performance, achieving state-of-the-art results in generation quality, physical consistency, and generalization ability.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that naive multi-view LAM training is insufficient for 3D awareness due to appearance leakage and inter-camera discrepancies, but with tightly coupled geometric and reconstruction constraints, learned latent actions can achieve 3D awareness and substantially improve world model capabilities for embodied intelligence.

title: One Ranking, Any Budget: Matryoshka Evidence-to-Context Frame Selection for Long-Video Understanding
summary: Frame selection is essential for applying Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) to long videos due to severe frame redundancy and limited context windows. Since the appropriate frame budget varies with the downstream LMM, reasoning demands, and latency constraints, a practical selector should serve multiple budgets. However, existing methods typically optimize an isolated frame subset for each predefined budget: when the budget changes, previously selected evidence may be replaced rather than progressively augmented. Ranking frames by a fixed score would allow prefix reuse across budgets, but it ignores the distinct roles of different ranking positions. In this paper, we formulate long-video frame selection as a Matryoshka ranking problem: constructing a single priority sequence whose small prefixes concentrate query-conditioned evidence, while progressively larger prefixes preserve this evidence and add broader temporal context. Efficiently constructing such a ranking is itself challenging, as densely sampling long videos and evaluating frame-query relevance incurs substantial overhead. We therefore introduce Matryoshka Evidence-to-Context (MEC) Frame Selection, a training-free framework that builds a reusable sparse video index, discovers candidates through sparse probing and local zooming, and greedily constructs a position-adaptive ranking: early positions emphasize evidence; later positions progressively favor temporal coverage while preserving visual diversity. A single ranking can thus be truncated to any target budget without rerunning the selector. Across four benchmarks and six frame budgets, MEC improves average accuracy over uniform sampling by 3.77 percentage points, matches strong state-of-the-art selectors, and reduces end-to-end selection latency by 47.37-51.19%.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Matryoshka Evidence-to-Context (MEC) Frame Selection, a training-free framework that constructs a single reusable priority sequence of frames from long videos, where small prefixes concentrate on query-relevant evidence and larger prefixes add broader temporal context. A single ranking can be truncated to any budget without rerunning, improving accuracy over uniform sampling by 3.77 points while reducing latency by 47-51%.
AI.motivation: Existing frame selection methods optimize an isolated subset for each predefined budget, so changing budgets replaces previously selected evidence instead of progressively augmenting it. Fixed-score ranking enables prefix reuse but ignores the distinct roles of different ranking positions (evidence vs. context), and dense sampling of long videos is computationally expensive.
AI.method: MEC formulates frame selection as a Matryoshka ranking problem: building one priority sequence where small prefixes concentrate query-conditioned evidence and larger prefixes preserve that evidence while adding broader temporal context. The training-free framework builds a reusable sparse video index, discovers candidates via sparse probing and local zooming, and greedily constructs a position-adaptive ranking where early positions emphasize evidence and later positions balance temporal coverage with visual diversity.
AI.result: Across four benchmarks and six frame budgets, MEC improves average accuracy over uniform sampling by 3.77 percentage points, matches strong state-of-the-art selectors, and reduces end-to-end selection latency by 47.37-51.19%.
AI.conclusion: A single Matryoshka-style priority ranking can serve multiple frame budgets simultaneously without rerunning the selector, proving that long-video frame selection can be made both high-quality and efficient by distinguishing evidence-concentrated early positions from context-expanding later positions.

title: Iterative Hybrid Discrete-Continuous Viewpoint Planning for UAV Photogrammetry
comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables. Accepted for publication at the 14th IEEE European Conference on Visual Information Processing (EUVIP 2026)
summary: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) photogrammetry requires camera networks that provide sufficient surface coverage, image overlap, parallax, and resolution, yet conventional flight patterns are often poorly adapted to scene geometry resulting in local reconstruction errors. This paper proposes an iterative hybrid discrete-continuous viewpoint planning method for targeted UAV photogrammetry from a proxy reconstruction. The method scores sampled surface points using photogrammetric heuristics based on frontality, imaging distance, parallax, and multi-view observation count, while also evaluating the full viewpoint set in terms of visibility, pairwise overlap, and graph connectivity. Candidate viewpoints are generated around weakly observed regions, refined using clustered Covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES) optimisation, and removed when redundant. The final flight path combines close-range detail viewpoints with wider model-coverage viewpoints, balancing local reconstruction quality with global image-network robustness. Evaluation on three synthetic scenes shows that the proposed method improves both reconstruction accuracy and completeness compared with prior UAV path-planning methods.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an iterative hybrid discrete-continuous viewpoint planning method for targeted UAV photogrammetry, which uses photogrammetric heuristics to score surface points, optimizes candidate viewpoints around weakly observed regions via CMA-ES, and combines close-range detail views with wider coverage views. It improves reconstruction accuracy and completeness over prior methods on three synthetic scenes.
AI.motivation: Conventional UAV flight patterns are poorly adapted to scene geometry, leading to local reconstruction errors due to insufficient coverage, overlap, parallax, and resolution in camera networks.
AI.method: The method iteratively plans viewpoints using a hybrid discrete-continuous approach: (1) scores sampled surface points with photogrammetric heuristics (frontality, imaging distance, parallax, multi-view observation count); (2) evaluates the full viewpoint set for visibility, pairwise overlap, and graph connectivity; (3) generates candidate viewpoints around weakly observed regions; (4) refines them with clustered CMA-ES optimization; (5) removes redundant viewpoints. The final flight path blends close-range detail viewpoints with wide model-coverage viewpoints.
AI.result: Evaluation on three synthetic scenes demonstrates that the proposed method improves both reconstruction accuracy and completeness compared with prior UAV path-planning methods.
AI.conclusion: The proposed iterative hybrid discrete-continuous viewpoint planning approach effectively balances local reconstruction quality with global image-network robustness, outperforming existing UAV path-planning techniques in targeted photogrammetry.

title: PhyLatent: Learning Dynamics-Relevant Representations for JEPA World Models
summary: We propose PhyLatent, a dynamics-relevant training objective for JointEmbedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) world models. Our key observation is that preventing global latent collapse does not ensure that a representation preserves physical states and action consequences. We identify three failure modes in JEPA world models: physical invariance collapse, physical identifiability collapse, and counterfactual dynamics collapse. PhyLatent addresses them through three training pathways: physical invariance, physical identifiability, and counterfactual dynamics, implemented with physical state grounding, future representation alignment, static visual invariance, counterfactual branch separation, and latent denoising. On OGBench-Cube, PhyLatent reduces the three failure rates from 15.60%, 6.71%, and 8.41% to 7.53%, 0.95%, and 4.62%, respectively, and improves model predictive control (MPC) success from 70.0% to 78.1%. With the same architecture and planner, it further improves success from 81.0% to 98.0% on TwoRooms and remains competitive on Reacher and PushT. These results show that global non-collapse alone is insufficient for learning a reliable JEPA worldmodel state space.

AI.tldr: PhyLatent introduces a dynamics-relevant training objective for JEPA world models, addressing three specific collapse failure modes (physical invariance, physical identifiability, and counterfactual dynamics) through three training pathways. It significantly reduces failure rates on OGBench-Cube and improves MPC success across multiple benchmarks, demonstrating that global non-collapse alone is insufficient for reliable world model learning.
AI.motivation: The paper identifies that while existing JEPA world models prevent global latent collapse, this does not guarantee that learned representations preserve physical states and action consequences. Three specific failure modes are identified: physical invariance collapse, physical identifiability collapse, and counterfactual dynamics collapse.
AI.method: PhyLatent implements three training pathways—physical invariance, physical identifiability, and counterfactual dynamics—using techniques including physical state grounding, future representation alignment, static visual invariance, counterfactual branch separation, and latent denoising.
AI.result: On OGBench-Cube, PhyLatent reduces three failure rates from 15.60%, 6.71%, and 8.41% to 7.53%, 0.95%, and 4.62% respectively, and improves MPC success from 70.0% to 78.1%. It further improves success from 81.0% to 98.0% on TwoRooms and remains competitive on Reacher and PushT.
AI.conclusion: Global non-collapse alone is insufficient for learning a reliable JEPA world model state space—explicitly addressing physical and dynamics-related collapse modes is necessary for robust world model representations.

title: Engram-E2VID: Reference-Based Event-to-Video Reconstruction via Generative Activation of Appearance Engrams
summary: Reference-based event-to-video reconstruction aims to recover target RGB frames from a reference frame and the event stream captured over the reference-to-target interval. Although events provide fine-grained temporal cues, they encode sparse and asynchronous log-intensity changes rather than absolute appearance, making faithful reconstruction intrinsically challenging. The central challenge lies in associating event-derived target-time structures with relevant appearance information from the reference frame, especially under complex motion and long temporal intervals. In this work, we propose Engram-E2VID, a structure-guided framework that reconstructs target frames through the generative activation of appearance engrams. Specifically, the reference frame is encoded into token-space appearance engrams, while the event stream and reference context are transformed into a target-time motion-structure scaffold that captures motion boundaries and event-induced structural changes. Within a one-step diffusion backbone, scaffold-derived structural tokens progressively interact with and activate relevant appearance engrams across layers. This token-space association allows target structures to access reference appearance without relying on direct pixel-wise correspondence, while the diffusion prior complements uncertain or newly revealed regions. Across three benchmarks, Engram-E2VID improves PSNR by up to 3.29 dB and reduces LPIPS by up to 0.08 over the strongest same-input baseline, while degrading more slowly as the reconstruction interval increases.

AI.tldr: Engram-E2VID is a structure-guided framework for reference-based event-to-video reconstruction that encodes reference frames into token-space appearance engrams and transforms event streams into motion-structure scaffolds, then uses a one-step diffusion backbone to iteratively activate relevant appearance engrams, achieving up to 3.29 dB PSNR improvement and 0.08 LPIPS reduction over baselines.
AI.motivation: Events capture sparse and asynchronous log-intensity changes rather than absolute appearance, making faithful reconstruction from a reference frame and event stream intrinsically challenging. The key difficulty is associating event-derived target-time structures with relevant appearance information from the reference frame, especially under complex motion and long temporal intervals.
AI.method: The reference frame is encoded into token-space appearance engrams, while the event stream and reference context are transformed into a target-time motion-structure scaffold capturing motion boundaries and structural changes. A one-step diffusion backbone allows scaffold-derived structural tokens to progressively interact with and activate relevant appearance engrams across layers, enabling token-space association without direct pixel-wise correspondence.
AI.result: Across three benchmarks, Engram-E2VID improves PSNR by up to 3.29 dB and reduces LPIPS by up to 0.08 over the strongest same-input baseline, while degrading more slowly as the reconstruction interval increases.
AI.conclusion: Token-space association between target structures and reference appearance, combined with a diffusion prior for handling uncertain or newly revealed regions, provides an effective paradigm for reference-based event-to-video reconstruction that is more robust to longer temporal intervals.

title: LiteKD-Net: Lightweight Knowledge-Distilled Network for Mobile Image Denoising
summary: Mobile image denoising requires both good restoration quality and low computational cost. In addition, it's annoying to collect large-scale LQ-GT clean pairs. As a result, we propose LiteKD-Net, a lightweight knowledge-distilled network for mobile image denoising. First, a physics-guided noise simulation pipeline generates paired training data by adding pixel crosstalk compared with pipelines applied to cameras. Next, we adapt the Real-ESRGAN to identity-resolution denoising and construct a lightweight Student using Lite-RRDB blocks based on depthwise separable convolutions. Third, feature-level knowledge distillation is applied to transfer the Teacher's restoration capability to the Student without introducing additional inference cost. Experiments on real-world datasets show that our model reaches great reduction in runtime and increase in the inference rate with good restoration quality. Our model also reaches the best in all metrics compared with SwinIR. These results indicate that LiteKD-Net provides a great trade-off between restoration quality and computational efficiency.

AI.tldr: LiteKD-Net is a lightweight knowledge-distilled network for mobile image denoising that uses a physics-guided noise simulation pipeline for training data generation, a Lite-RRDB student network based on depthwise separable convolutions, and feature-level knowledge distillation from a Real-ESRGAN teacher to achieve efficient real-time denoising with minimal computational cost.
AI.motivation: Mobile image denoising requires both high restoration quality and low computational cost, but collecting large-scale low-quality/clean training pairs is difficult and existing methods are computationally heavy for mobile deployment.
AI.method: The approach has three components: (1) a physics-guided noise simulation pipeline that generates paired training data with pixel crosstalk beyond typical camera pipelines; (2) a lightweight Student network built with Lite-RRDB blocks using depthwise separable convolutions for identity-resolution denoising, adapted from Real-ESRGAN; (3) feature-level knowledge distillation to transfer the Teacher's restoration capability to the Student without extra inference cost.
AI.result: Experiments on real-world datasets show significant runtime reduction and increased inference rate while maintaining good restoration quality. The model achieves the best performance across all metrics compared to SwinIR.
AI.conclusion: LiteKD-Net offers a great trade-off between restoration quality and computational efficiency, making it suitable for mobile image denoising applications.

title: ConceptADapt: Concept-guided Adaptive Feature Reconstruction with Dynamic Attention for Few-Shot Industrial Anomaly Detection
summary: Few-shot industrial anomaly detection (FS-IAD) focuses on detecting and localizing visual defects in industrial inspection during the cold-start phase, where only a limited number of normal training samples are available per category. Recent advances in this field predominantly leverage visual features from foundation-model and have achieved promising performance. Despite the strong representational power of foundation-model features, the model generalization remains fragile due to the extreme scarcity of normal training data.To address this pivotal issue, we propose ConceptADapt, a concept-guided adaptive feature reconstruction model with dynamic attention. Specifically, our model pre-learns a set of fixed normal concepts from the limited support features and leverages them to mine relationships with query features, thereby recalibrating their statistics for improved anomaly detection at test time. To mitigate the prevalent feature shortcut problem, which is particularly severe under low-data regimes, we further develop a dynamic attention mechanism integrated with sparse autoencoders to learn robust normal concepts during training. Moreover, to enable fast adaptation during inference, our model remains lightweight by incorporating LoRA into the attention module, which introduces only minimal updating parameters.Extensive experiments on three widely adopted FS-IAD benchmarks, including MVTec-AD, VisA, and MPDD, demonstrate that our model consistently outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) approaches across both detection and localization tasks, achieving significant improvements under various shot settings.

AI.tldr: ConceptADapt is a concept-guided adaptive feature reconstruction model for few-shot industrial anomaly detection that pre-learns fixed normal concepts from limited support features, uses dynamic attention with sparse autoencoders to learn robust concepts, and employs LoRA for lightweight fast adaptation, achieving SOTA results on MVTec-AD, VisA, and MPDD.
AI.motivation: Few-shot industrial anomaly detection (FS-IAD) suffers from fragile model generalization due to extreme scarcity of normal training data, even when leveraging powerful foundation-model features. The paper addresses this pivotal generalization issue in low-data regimes.
AI.method: The proposed ConceptADapt pre-learns a set of fixed normal concepts from limited support features to mine relationships with query features and recalibrate their statistics. It integrates a dynamic attention mechanism with sparse autoencoders to learn robust normal concepts and mitigate feature shortcut problems. LoRA is incorporated into the attention module for lightweight inference-time adaptation with minimal updating parameters.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on three benchmarks (MVTec-AD, VisA, MPDD) show consistent state-of-the-art performance improvements over existing approaches across both anomaly detection and localization tasks, under various few-shot settings.
AI.conclusion: ConceptADapt effectively addresses the limited-data generalization challenge in FS-IAD by combining concept-guided feature recalibration, dynamic attention with sparse autoencoders, and LoRA-based lightweight adaptation, outperforming prior methods on multiple benchmarks.

title: UniVVT: A Unified End-to-End Framework for High-Fidelity Video Virtual Try-on
summary: Video Virtual Try-On (VVT) synthesizes a video of a person wearing a target garment while preserving identity, motion, and scene dynamics. Dominant approaches cast VVT as mask-conditioned video inpainting and rely on separate modules for human parsing, pose estimation, and garment warping. This multi-stage design complicates deployment and, more critically, allows errors in explicit geometric priors to propagate irreversibly into the generated video. We present UniVVT, a unified end-to-end framework that reframes VVT as semantically conditioned video generation, eliminating mask, pose, and warping modules at inference. At its core, a scene-task perceiver built on a Multimodal Large Language Model jointly encodes the source video, target garment, and task instruction into compact, task-aware latent tokens, implicitly capturing what to transfer and where and how to transfer it. A lightweight semantic bridge then aligns these tokens with the conditioning space of a diffusion-based video generator, enabling coherent garment transfer. To robustly couple the heterogeneous components, we devise a three-stage progressive training strategy comprising semantic alignment, joint task adaptation, and flexible-resolution refinement. Extensive experiments demonstrate that UniVVT achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks, validating implicit semantic guidance as a simple and effective alternative to fragile geometric preprocessing for end-to-end virtual try-on.

AI.tldr: UniVVT is a unified end-to-end framework for Video Virtual Try-On that reframes the task as semantically conditioned video generation, eliminating the fragile mask, pose, and warping modules used in traditional multi-stage approaches. It uses a scene-task perceiver built on a Multimodal Large Language Model to encode source video, target garment, and task instruction into compact task-aware latent tokens, which are then aligned with a diffusion-based video generator via a lightweight semantic bridge. A three-stage progressive training strategy enables robust coupling of the heterogeneous components, achieving state-of-the-art performance.
AI.motivation: Existing VVT approaches rely on multi-stage pipelines with separate modules for human parsing, pose estimation, and garment warping, which complicate deployment and propagate errors from explicit geometric priors irreversibly into the generated video.
AI.method: UniVVT casts VVT as semantically conditioned video generation with a scene-task perceiver (built on MLLM) that encodes source video, target garment, and task instruction into compact task-aware latent tokens, a semantic bridge aligning these tokens with a diffusion-based video generator, and a three-stage progressive training strategy (semantic alignment, joint task adaptation, flexible-resolution refinement).
AI.result: UniVVT achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks, demonstrating that implicit semantic guidance is a simple and effective alternative to fragile geometric preprocessing for end-to-end virtual try-on.
AI.conclusion: UniVVT validates that implicit semantic guidance can replace explicit geometric priors in VVT, offering a unified, deployable end-to-end framework that achieves competitive results while eliminating error propagation from multi-stage geometric modules.

title: GST-Bench: Can VLMs Develop Global Spatial Awareness from Video?
summary: Spatial intelligence is fundamental to embodied agents, yet existing benchmarks focus on local spatial perception from single or few viewpoints, overlooking global spatial awareness over continuous, long-horizon visual streams. To address this limitation, we introduce the Global-Spatial-Temporal Benchmark (GST-Bench), a VQA benchmark for global spatial intelligence in video understanding, comprising human-verified questions derived from 6,790 minutes of synthetically generated video. It requires models to perform accurate spatial inference from novel viewpoints unseen in the input video and to map egocentric observations onto global top-down images. A comprehensive evaluation of 22 state-of-the-art VLMs exposes a striking gap between models and humans: the strongest zero-shot model attains only 42.68, far below the human score of 79.08. To probe the cause of this gap, we construct GST-Bench-Local and find that models, despite strong local spatial understanding under the same task formulation, still fail to consolidate long-horizon observations into a globally consistent scene representation. We further provide GST-Train, a dataset for global spatial reasoning, as a complementary resource to facilitate future research on this challenge.

AI.tldr: Introduces GST-Bench, a VQA benchmark for global spatial intelligence in video understanding that tests models on spatial inference from novel viewpoints and mapping egocentric observations to top-down global views, revealing a large gap between the best VLM (42.68) and humans (79.08), and provides complementary training data (GST-Train).
AI.motivation: Existing benchmarks focus on local spatial perception from single or few viewpoints, overlooking global spatial awareness over continuous long-horizon visual streams, which is fundamental for embodied agents.
AI.method: Constructs GST-Bench from 6,790 minutes of synthetically generated video with human-verified questions requiring novel-viewpoint inference and egocentric-to-top-down mapping; evaluates 22 state-of-the-art VLMs; builds GST-Bench-Local to isolate local vs. global spatial reasoning; provides GST-Train as complementary training data.
AI.result: The strongest zero-shot VLM achieves only 42.68, far below the human score of 79.08; GST-Bench-Local shows models have strong local spatial understanding but fail to consolidate long-horizon observations into globally consistent scene representations.
AI.conclusion: There is a striking gap between VLMs and humans in global spatial intelligence, and the bottleneck lies in consolidating long-horizon observations into global scene representations rather than local spatial understanding; GST-Train is provided to facilitate future research.

title: Beyond Relevance: Bayesian Evidence Acquisition for Agentic Whole-Slide Image Reasoning
summary: Whole-slide image (WSI) reasoning requires an agent to sequentially acquire visual evidence before answering a diagnostic question. Existing training-free agentic frameworks formulate this process as iterative patch retrieval based on semantic relevance to the question.
