However, semantic relevance does not necessarily imply diagnostic informativeness in computational pathology, where competing diagnoses often exhibit similar and overlapping morphological patterns, making many patches semantically relevant yet diagnostically non-discriminative. Consequently, relevance-based retrieval may acquire redundant observations and leave diagnostic uncertainty unresolved. We propose BEACON, a plug-and-play agentic framework that reformulates WSI reasoning as a Bayesian evidence acquisition problem. BEACON maintains a probabilistic belief over competing diagnostic hypotheses and sequentially acquires patches by maximizing expected information gain (EIG) to reduce diagnostic uncertainty. An evidence controller then determines whether to answer, acquire additional evidence, or perform higher-resolution inspection. Built entirely from off-the-shelf foundation models, BEACON requires no additional training or fine-tuning. Extensive zero-shot experiments across five WSI-VQA benchmarks demonstrate that BEACON achieves the strongest overall performance among training-free agentic frameworks while substantially improving evidence acquisition efficiency, establishing Bayesian evidence acquisition as a principled paradigm for uncertainty-aware agentic WSI reasoning. The code is available at https://github.com/bryanwong17/BEACON

AI.tldr: BEACON is a plug-and-play, training-free agentic framework for whole-slide image (WSI) reasoning that reformulates the task as Bayesian evidence acquisition, sequentially selecting patches by maximizing expected information gain (EIG) to reduce diagnostic uncertainty, and achieves state-of-the-art performance among training-free methods across five WSI-VQA benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing training-free agentic frameworks for WSI reasoning retrieve patches based on semantic relevance to the diagnostic question, but semantic relevance does not guarantee diagnostic informativeness in computational pathology—competing diagnoses often share overlapping morphological patterns, so relevance-based retrieval acquires redundant observations and leaves diagnostic uncertainty unresolved.
AI.method: BEACON maintains a probabilistic belief over competing diagnostic hypotheses and sequentially acquires patches by maximizing expected information gain (EIG). An evidence controller decides whether to answer, acquire more evidence, or perform higher-resolution inspection. It is built entirely from off-the-shelf foundation models with no additional training or fine-tuning.
AI.result: Extensive zero-shot experiments across five WSI-VQA benchmarks show BEACON achieves the strongest overall performance among training-free agentic frameworks while substantially improving evidence acquisition efficiency.
AI.conclusion: Bayesian evidence acquisition is established as a principled paradigm for uncertainty-aware agentic WSI reasoning, outperforming relevance-based retrieval approaches without requiring training.

title: Flow-Map Distillation on Relation Manifolds for Image Restoration
comment: 9 pages, 7 figures. Accepted to ACM Multimedia 2026
summary: Knowledge distillation for image restoration typically aligns intermediate features or relation matrices between teacher and student networks as static targets, ignoring the dynamic structure of the knowledge transfer process. In this paper, we propose Flow-Map Distillation on Relation Manifolds (FoRM), which reformulates relation-based knowledge transfer as a continuous flow mapping problem on the relation manifold. Rather than regressing a constant velocity field between student and teacher relation states, FoRM learns a flow map operator $\mathcal{F}_θ(\mathbf{z}, t, s)$ that directly predicts the relation state at any target time $s$ given the current state at time $t$, enabling richer trajectory-level supervision. To ensure global self-consistency of the learned flow map, we introduce a safe semigroup consistency constraint that enforces compositional agreement using ground-truth bridge states, eliminating phantom-state error accumulation. An endpoint anchoring loss further prevents the operator from drifting away from the teacher target. Extensive experiments on five image restoration tasks, including super-resolution, deraining, denoising, deblurring, and low-light enhancement, demonstrate consistent gains over state-of-the-art distillation baselines across multiple backbone architectures, reducing training variance by approximately 50\% compared to naive flow matching distillation while achieving superior restoration quality.

AI.tldr: FoRM reformulates knowledge distillation for image restoration as a continuous flow-mapping problem on the relation manifold, learning a flow map operator that predicts relation states at any target time with a semigroup consistency constraint and endpoint anchoring to improve restoration quality and reduce training variance by ~50%.
AI.motivation: Existing knowledge distillation methods for image restoration treat intermediate features or relation matrices as static targets, ignoring the dynamic structure of the knowledge transfer process, which limits the richness of supervision.
AI.method: FoRM learns a flow map operator F_theta(z, t, s) that predicts the relation state at target time s given current state at time t, enabling trajectory-level supervision. It introduces a safe semigroup consistency constraint using ground-truth bridge states to ensure global self-consistency, plus an endpoint anchoring loss to prevent drift from the teacher target.
AI.result: Experiments on five image restoration tasks (super-resolution, deraining, denoising, deblurring, low-light enhancement) show consistent gains over state-of-the-art distillation baselines across multiple backbone architectures, with ~50% reduction in training variance compared to naive flow matching distillation while achieving superior restoration quality.
AI.conclusion: Modeling knowledge transfer as a continuous flow on the relation manifold with consistency constraints provides a more effective and stable distillation paradigm for image restoration.

title: HyTBE: Hyperbolic Target-Background Expert Model for Cross-Domain Infrared Small Target Detection
summary: Infrared small target detection (IRSTD) has achieved substantial progress under domain-consistent evaluation, yet detector performance often degrades markedly when generalizing to unseen infrared domains. Existing methods primarily improve detection by enhancing target responses and suppressing background interference. However, when trained on only a limited set of source domains, their learned decision rules are inevitably established from a restricted range of source-domain target-background relation patterns. We formulate this cross-domain failure as target-background relation shift: unseen domains may exhibit relation patterns that are not observed during training, thereby weakening the discriminative capability learned from the source domains. To address this problem, we propose HyTBE, a Hyperbolic Target-Background Expert model that expands source-domain relation patterns and adaptively adjusts visual representations using explicit relation cues. The Target-Background Relation Intervention selectively perturbs either targets or backgrounds, broadening the observable relation patterns during training while maintaining valid supervision. Subsequently, the Hyperbolic Relation Modeling maps multi-scale visual cues into a Poincaré ball and characterizes the target-background relation of each feature token according to its relative distances to the target and background anchors. The Hyperbolic-guided MoE Adapter further uses these hyperbolic relation representations to calibrate multi-scale visual features and aggregate expert-specific feature corrections for different relation patterns. Leave-one-domain-out experiments on NUAA-SIRST, NUDT-SIRST, and IRSTD-1K demonstrate that HyTBE achieves stronger cross-domain generalization than competitive baselines.

AI.tldr: HyTBE is a Hyperbolic Target-Background Expert model for infrared small target detection that addresses cross-domain generalization failure by modeling target-background relation patterns in hyperbolic space, using relation intervention during training, and calibrating multi-scale features via a hyperbolic-guided mixture-of-experts adapter.
AI.motivation: Infrared small target detection (IRSTD) methods fail to generalize to unseen infrared domains because they learn decision rules from a restricted range of source-domain target-background relation patterns. This cross-domain failure is formulated as target-background relation shift.
AI.method: Three components: (1) Target-Background Relation Intervention perturbs targets or backgrounds to broaden observable relation patterns during training; (2) Hyperbolic Relation Modeling maps multi-scale visual cues into a Poincaré ball and characterizes target-background relations via relative distances to target/background anchors; (3) Hyperbolic-guided MoE Adapter calibrates multi-scale visual features and aggregates expert-specific corrections for different relation patterns.
AI.result: Leave-one-domain-out experiments on NUAA-SIRST, NUDT-SIRST, and IRSTD-1K demonstrate that HyTBE achieves stronger cross-domain generalization than competitive baselines.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly modeling and expanding target-background relation patterns in hyperbolic space improves cross-domain generalization for infrared small target detection.

title: SR-JEPA: Learning Predictive Latent State in 3D Scenes
summary: Joint-embedding predictive architectures learn by predicting latent representations of missing observations, yet many masked JEPAs are evaluated primarily through the encoders they produce. We ask what a trained predictive pathway itself infers when an entire entity is absent from a native 3D scene. We introduce SR-JEPA, a point-native JEPA for scene-scale point clouds whose original frozen predictive pathway can be queried at a supplied location. At evaluation, every point of one object is removed before encoding and replaced by the same shape-free 32-point query at its centroid. Training uses only self-contained 3D EMA targets: no reconstruction, semantic labels, language, or lifted 2D features. On 5,953 held-out ARKitScenes objects, the imputed latent reaches 43.13% semantic-identity macro accuracy, 22.18 points above the strongest floor. Randomizing the prediction path removes 9.78 points, while substituting matched donor context removes 21.98 points. On 8,570 Sr3D support pairs, the full latent reaches 41.15 AP; identity decoded from the missing-object latent, combined with anchor identity and geometry, reaches 39.37 AP, leaving an unresolved 1.78-point residual. These results reveal a queryable, compositional 3D predictive state: the model completes context-dependent entity content, which downstream computation combines with metric geometry.

AI.tldr: SR-JEPA is a point-native JEPA for scene-scale point clouds whose frozen predictive pathway can be queried to impute latent representations of entirely missing objects. Through extensive evaluations on ARKitScenes and Sr3D, the paper shows that the predictive state encodes context-dependent semantic identity of absent entities (43.13% macro accuracy, significantly above baselines) and combines compositional content with metric geometry for downstream tasks.
AI.motivation: Most masked JEPAs are evaluated primarily through the encoders they produce, leaving an unexplored question: what does the trained predictive pathway itself infer when an entire entity is absent from a native 3D scene?
AI.method: SR-JEPA trains a point-native JEPA for scene-scale point clouds using only self-contained 3D EMA targets (no reconstruction, semantic labels, language, or 2D features). At evaluation, all points of one object are removed, and a shape-free 32-point query at its centroid is used to query the frozen predictive pathway.
AI.result: On 5,953 held-out ARKitScenes objects, the imputed latent reaches 43.13% semantic-identity macro accuracy (22.18 points above the strongest floor). Randomizing the prediction path removes 9.78 points, while substituted donor context removes 21.98 points. On 8,570 Sr3D support pairs, the full latent reaches 41.15 AP; identity decoded from the missing-object latent combined with anchor identity and geometry reaches 39.37 AP, leaving a 1.78-point residual.
AI.conclusion: The results reveal a queryable, compositional 3D predictive state: the model completes context-dependent entity content, which downstream computation combines with metric geometry.

title: Vorch-Director: Interactive World Story Model via Noise-Aware Error Rectification
summary: Autoregressive continuation provides a natural path toward minute-scale audio-visual generation by repeatedly extending a short-window generator conditioned on previously generated video and audio. However, models are trained on clean ground-truth histories, while inference relies on their own generated histories, where accumulated errors cause identity drift, over-smoothing, and audio-visual desynchronization. Recent methods reduce this mismatch by reusing prediction residuals as synthetic corruption, but we observe that the effectiveness of residual correction critically depends on the flow-matching noise level at which residuals are produced. We propose Vorch-Director, a noise-level-aware residual correction strategy that associates each residual with its originating noise level and injects residuals from matched noise regimes during training. By aligning injected errors with the denoising process, Vorch-Director produces more realistic autoregressive histories while retaining efficient teacher-forcing training. Built on the audio-visual LTX-2 diffusion transformer, Vorch-Director further introduces task embeddings to distinguish historical video, reference images, and target video, enabling unified conditioning for long-horizon generation. Together with a clean conditioning sink and mixed-task training, Vorch-Director supports multi-shot, multi-subject, reference-guided audio-visual long-video generation. We evaluate Vorch-Director on ST-Bench and introduce a new long-horizon audio-visual benchmark with metrics for quality drift and long-range consistency. Extensive experiments demonstrate improved stability and audio-visual fidelity over strong baselines.

AI.tldr: Vorchor-Director is a noise-level-aware residual correction strategy for autoregressive audio-visual generation that injects residuals from matched noise regimes during training to align synthetic corruption with the denoising process, reducing the train-inference mismatch that causes identity drift, over-smoothing, and audio-visual desynchronization in long-horizon generation.
AI.motivation: Autoregressive continuation models for minute-scale audio-visual generation suffer from a train-inference mismatch: they are trained on clean ground-truth histories but must generate from their own (error-prone) histories at inference, leading to accumulated errors such as identity drift, over-smoothing, and audio-visual desynchronization. Prior residual-correction methods are limited because their effectiveness depends on the flow-matching noise level at which residuals are produced.
AI.method: Vorchor-Director associates each residual with its originating noise level and injects residuals from matched noise regimes during training, aligning injected errors with the denoising process. Built on the audio-visual LTX-2 diffusion transformer, it introduces task embeddings to distinguish historical video, reference images, and target video, enabling unified conditioning. It also employs a clean conditioning sink and mixed-task training for multi-shot, multi-subject, reference-guided generation.
AI.result: Evaluated on ST-Bench and a newly introduced long-horizon audio-visual benchmark (with metrics for quality drift and long-range consistency), Vorchor-Director demonstrates improved stability and audio-visual fidelity over strong baselines.
AI.conclusion: Noise-level-aware residual correction effectively bridges the train-inference gap in autoregressive audio-visual generation, enabling more stable and faithful long-horizon generation without sacrificing efficient teacher-forcing training.

title: Evidence-Driven Dynamic Visual Selector for Efficient Long Video Understanding
summary: Recent advancements in MLLM-based long-form video understanding have mitigated inference-time computational cost and limited context lengths by selecting query-relevant frames. However, existing approaches predominantly rely on external proxy scorers and rigid heuristic rules, inevitably suffering from misalignment with the target MLLM's intrinsic evidence and failing to accommodate the non-uniform spatiotemporal information density. In this paper, we propose a fine-grained dynamic visual selection framework named EviSelect, grounded in the target MLLM internal attention evidence. Our method efficiently probes visual evidence via sparse prefilling as a structured prior to guide distribution-aware dynamic sampling. Specifically, we efficiently approximate attention maps of the target MLLM using highly compressed visual inputs and sparse attention, well-aligned to the full counterpart. Conditioned on three complementary attention components derived from this prior, we design a lightweight selector that not only precisely locates query-relevant timestamps but also adaptively adjusts the local sampling rate and spatial resolution. To enable evidence-conditioned spatiotemporal sampling, we formulate the selector as a stochastic policy and optimize it via GRPO under a joint accuracy--efficiency reward. By rewarding correct predictions under lower visual cost through group-relative comparisons, our method encourages the policy to allocate computation dynamically according to the information density of each video. Across three long video understanding benchmarks, EviSelect achieves superior performance compared to existing methods while reducing selected visual tokens by about 50\% and achieving a 3.9x end-to-end speedup.

AI.tldr: EviSelect is a fine-grained dynamic visual selection framework for long-form video understanding that uses the target MLLM's internal attention evidence to guide distribution-aware dynamic sampling. It approximates attention maps via sparse prefilling, uses a lightweight stochastic policy selector optimized with GRPO under a joint accuracy-efficiency reward, and achieves superior performance with ~50% fewer visual tokens and 3.9x speedup.
AI.motivation: Existing MLLM-based long-form video understanding methods rely on external proxy scorers and rigid heuristic rules for frame selection, which misalign with the target MLLM's intrinsic evidence and fail to handle non-uniform spatiotemporal information density across videos.
AI.method: EviSelect probes the target MLLM's internal attention evidence via sparse prefilling as a structured prior, approximating attention maps using highly compressed visual inputs and sparse attention. From this prior, three complementary attention components are derived and used by a lightweight selector to locate query-relevant timestamps while adaptively adjusting local sampling rate and spatial resolution. The selector is formulated as a stochastic policy optimized via GRPO under a joint accuracy-efficiency reward that rewards correct predictions under lower visual cost.
AI.result: Across three long video understanding benchmarks, EviSelect achieves superior performance compared to existing methods while reducing selected visual tokens by about 50% and achieving a 3.9x end-to-end speedup.
AI.conclusion: EviSelect demonstrates that grounding visual selection in the target MLLM's intrinsic attention evidence—rather than external proxies—enables more accurate and efficient long-form video understanding, with computation dynamically allocated according to each video's information density.

title: VSMP-IMU: Video-Grounded Semantic Motion Programs for Sensor-Aware Synthetic IMU Generation
summary: Wearable human activity recognition (HAR) is often limited by the scarcity of labeled sensor data, especially in low-resource, class-imbalanced, and subject-generalization settings. Synthetic IMU generation can reduce this dependency and enhance HAR machine learning model's performance, but existing approaches face a trade-off without addressing all factors: video-driven methods are visually grounded but sensitive to pose-estimation errors, while text-driven methods are controllable but often weakly grounded in how activities are actually performed. We present VSMP-IMU, a video-grounded framework for controllable synthetic IMU generation based on a structured Semantic Motion Program (SMP), which separates activity-defining semantics from label-preserving variation. Given an input video, VSMP-IMU extracts and augments an SMP, uses it to synthesize motion, converts the motion into virtual IMU signals, and grounds the resulting signals to the target wearable domain. We evaluate VSMP-IMU against state-of-the-art synthetic data generation methods on five public IMU-HAR datasets under leave-one-person-out evaluation. VSMP-IMU achieves an average Macro-F1 of 78.33%, improving over real-only training by 9.77% and over the strongest prior synthetic baseline by 4.04%. In low-resource settings with reduced training data-samples, it improves over real-only training by 18.54% and over the strongest prior synthetic baselines by more than 6% on average. Under long-tail evaluation in imbalanced datasets, it improves tail-class Macro-F1 by 19.86% over Real-only training and by 4.76% over SOTA. These results show that structured video-grounded semantics provide a practical foundation for controllable, wearable-relevant synthetic sensor data generation.

AI.tldr: VSMP-IMU is a video-grounded framework for controllable synthetic IMU generation that uses a structured Semantic Motion Program (SMP) to separate activity semantics from label-preserving variation. It outperforms real-only training by 9.77% and prior synthetic baselines by 4.04% in Macro-F1 across five public IMU-HAR datasets under leave-one-person-out evaluation, with even larger gains in low-resource and long-tail settings.
AI.motivation: Wearable HAR suffers from scarcity of labeled sensor data, especially in low-resource, class-imbalanced, and subject-generalization settings. While synthetic IMU generation can mitigate this, existing approaches face a trade-off: video-driven methods are visually grounded but sensitive to pose-estimation errors, while text-driven methods are controllable but weakly grounded in actual activity performance. Existing methods fail to address all factors simultaneously.
AI.method: VSMP-IMU extracts and augments a structured Semantic Motion Program (SMP) from input video, which separates activity-defining semantics from label-preserving variation. The framework synthesizes motion from the SMP, converts it into virtual IMU signals, and grounds the resulting signals to the target wearable domain.
AI.result: VSMP-IMU achieves an average Macro-F1 of 78.33%, improving over real-only training by 9.77% and over the strongest prior synthetic baseline by 4.04%. In low-resource settings it improves by 18.54% over real-only and >6% over prior synthetic baselines. Under long-tail evaluation, it improves tail-class Macro-F1 by 19.86% over real-only and 4.76% over SOTA.
AI.conclusion: Structured video-grounded semantics provide a practical foundation for controllable, wearable-relevant synthetic sensor data generation, effectively addressing the trade-offs of prior video-driven and text-driven approaches across multiple evaluation settings.

title: KVAE: Family of Tokenizers for Multimodal Generative Models
summary: Latent diffusion modeling (LDM), a prominent paradigm, utilizes tokenizers to map input signal to compressed representation. This dependency positions tokenizer as an integral part of generation process itself, since it affects learning speed, quality of synthesized samples and lay foundation for later applications. This report presents series of KVAE tokenizers for audio, image and video, all designed for subsequent text-conditioned generation: KVAE-Audio, a continuous full-band 48 kHz tokenizer with a 50 Hz latent of 64 channels; KVAE-3D -- two causal video tokenizers for 4x16x16 and 4x8x8 compression; KVAE-2D, an image model, compressing input by factor of 8 with 32 channels. We demonstrate that reconstruction (PSNR, LPIPS, PESQ, etc.) and generation results on objective (Frechet Distance, CLIP score, CLAP score, etc.) and subjective (side-by-side evaluation) metrics matches or surpasses frontier opensource tokenizers, such as VAEs from Wan-2.2, HunyuanVideo-1.5, FLUX.2, MovieGen, StableAudio and MMAudio. Considering difficulty of development, we share with community training details, model selection method and ablation on design choices. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/kandinskylab/kvae and https://github.com/kandinskylab/kvae-audio.

AI.tldr: This report presents KVAE, a family of tokenizers for audio, image, and video designed for text-conditioned generation, including KVAE-Audio (48 kHz, 64 channels at 50 Hz), KVAE-3D (causal video tokenizers), and KVAE-2D (image compression by factor 8). These tokenizers match or surpass frontier open-source tokenizers across objective and subjective metrics.
AI.motivation: Latent diffusion models depend on tokenizers to map input signals to compressed representations, making the tokenizer a critical component that affects learning speed, sample quality, and downstream applications. There is a need for high-quality tokenizers across multiple modalities tailored for text-conditioned generation.
AI.method: The paper designs and develops a series of KVAE tokenizers: KVAE-Audio (continuous full-band 48 kHz tokenizer with 50 Hz latent and 64 channels), KVAE-3D (two causal video tokenizers for 4x16x16 and 4x8x8 compression), and KVAE-2D (image model compressing by factor 8 with 32 channels). It also shares training details, model selection methods, and ablation studies on design choices.
AI.result: Evaluation on reconstruction metrics (PSNR, LPIPS, PESQ) and generation metrics (Frechet Distance, CLIP score, CLAP score, side-by-side evaluation) shows KVAE matches or surpasses frontier open-source tokenizers including VAEs from Wan-2.2, HunyuanVideo-1.5, FLUX.2, MovieGen, StableAudio, and MMAudio.
AI.conclusion: The KVAE tokenizer family achieves competitive or superior performance compared to leading open-source tokenizers across audio, image, and video modalities, with open-sourced code and detailed training guidance to support community development.

title: Vorch-Omni: Multi-Task Orchestration of Sight and Sound
summary: Recent advances in generative video modeling have enabled diverse generation, reference-based synthesis, extension, and editing, but existing approaches often rely on fragmented task-specific models. A general model must distinguish heterogeneous target, source, and reference signals to determine what to generate, preserve, or use as guidance, while reducing interference among tasks. Joint audio-visual generation further increases this challenge by introducing diverse conditioning and output configurations across modalities. We present Vorch-Omni, a unified multi-task framework for audio-visual synthesis based on an arbitrary-condition-to-arbitrary-output formulation. It flexibly treats video and audio signals as either conditioning inputs or generation targets. Token-level conditioning masks and task identifiers distinguish targets, source content, and references, while position types separate temporal context from independent conditions. To capture semantic and structural information, Vorch-Omni employs complementary visual conditioning pathways: a vision-language model interprets sampled frames with text instructions, and a video VAE encodes conditions into latent tokens for direct guidance. We further build a distributed data pipeline to curate diverse temporally aligned audio-visual clips, generate structured captions and metadata, and balance heterogeneous task distributions. Built on a single flow-matching diffusion transformer without task-specific architectural changes, Vorch-Omni supports over 10 tasks, including text-to-video, text-to-audio-video, image- and reference-conditioned generation, temporal extension, audio-driven generation, video transformation, and audio-visual editing. This unified framework provides a scalable foundation for general-purpose audio-visual generation and manipulation.

AI.tldr: Vorch-Omni is a unified multi-task framework for audio-visual synthesis that treats video and audio as either conditioning inputs or generation targets, supporting over 10 tasks including text-to-video, audio-visual generation, editing, and extension using a single flow-matching diffusion transformer without task-specific architectural changes.
AI.motivation: Existing generative video approaches rely on fragmented task-specific models, but a general model must distinguish heterogeneous target, source, and reference signals, reduce interference among tasks, and handle diverse conditioning/output configurations across modalities in joint audio-visual generation.
AI.method: Uses an arbitrary-condition-to-arbitrary-output formulation with token-level conditioning masks and task identifiers to distinguish targets, sources, and references; position types separate temporal context from independent conditions; complementary visual conditioning pathways (vision-language model for semantic interpretation and video VAE for latent token guidance); a distributed data pipeline for curated temporally-aligned clips and balanced task distributions; built on a single flow-matching diffusion transformer.
AI.result: Supports over 10 tasks including text-to-video, text-to-audio-video, image- and reference-conditioned generation, temporal extension, audio-driven generation, video transformation, and audio-visual editing, all within a single unified framework.
AI.conclusion: The unified framework provides a scalable foundation for general-purpose audio-visual generation and manipulation.

title: Ordered Diffusion for 3D Human Registration
summary: 3D human registration has historically been treated as a regression task, assuming a unique ground-truth alignment exists between the template and an input point cloud. In reality, acquisition noise, occlusions, and unknown soft tissue dynamics introduce inherent ambiguity into human scans. Regression-based methods consequently converge to an average prediction, often failing to represent a plausible geometry. In our work, we embrace such uncertainty by modeling the registration as a distribution of alignments. We propose ODin, which formulates registration as a 3D diffusion process that generates a point cloud aligned with the target geometry while preserving template semantics through consistent point ordering. To achieve this, ODin relies on global, local, and positional conditioning, guiding each point to its correct location. Our experiments demonstrate that such a generative formulation not only outperforms its regression-based baseline, but also establishes a new state of the art, surpassing highly engineered methods while reducing the registration time by two-thirds. Pre-trained models and code are available at https://riccardomarin.github.io/odin/.

AI.tldr: ODin treats 3D human registration as a generative diffusion process rather than regression, modeling the inherent uncertainty in aligning a template to noisy/occluded point clouds, and achieves state-of-the-art results while reducing registration time by two-thirds.
AI.motivation: Traditional 3D human registration is treated as a regression task with a unique ground-truth alignment, but real-world scans contain ambiguity from noise, occlusions, and soft tissue dynamics. Regression methods converge to average predictions that often fail to represent plausible geometry.
AI.method: ODin formulates registration as a 3D diffusion process that generates a point cloud aligned with the target geometry while preserving template semantics through consistent point ordering. It uses global, local, and positional conditioning to guide each point to its correct location.
AI.result: The generative formulation outperforms its regression-based baseline and establishes a new state of the art, surpassing highly engineered methods while reducing registration time by two-thirds.
AI.conclusion: Modeling registration as a distribution of alignments via diffusion embraces uncertainty in human scans and produces more plausible geometries than traditional regression-based approaches, with improved performance and efficiency.

title: STAIL: Semantic Text-Anchored Incremental Learning for Medical Imaging via Large Language Models
summary: Deep learning models applied to medical image analysis suffer from severe catastrophic forgetting when continually adapting to new clinical tasks in dynamic environments. Mainstream incremental learning methods typically mitigate this by rehearsing raw historical images. However, this pixel-level rehearsal incurs significant storage overhead, raises privacy concerns, and fails to adequately capture the true data distribution with sparse exemplars. Inspired by human cognitive mechanisms, we propose a novel framework termed Semantic Text-Anchored Incremental Learning (STAIL) for sequential clinical tasks. To overcome the rehearsal bottleneck, STAIL introduces an asymmetric semantic consolidation buffer (SCB). By incorporating a minimal set of image anchors and extensive textual descriptions, the SCB enables dense semantic reconstruction of old tasks at a minimal storage cost. Furthermore, we design an LLM-derived Semantic Anchoring Mechanism (LSAM) that leverages the stable semantic space of frozen large language models as developmental priors. This mechanism explicitly anchors evolving visual features to textual representations, guiding and constraining plasticity and stability at both macroscopic and microscopic levels. Extensive experiments across three heterogeneous medical datasets, covering fundus, ultrasound, and X-ray imaging, demonstrate that STAIL acts as a highly effective plug-and-play module. It comprehensively enhances the performance of various existing baselines, achieving average gains of 2.24\% in AAA-AUC for sustained performance and 3.55\% in BWT-AUC for reduced forgetting. Code is available.

AI.tldr: STAIL is a semantic text-anchored incremental learning framework that addresses catastrophic forgetting in medical image analysis by replacing raw image rehearsal with a minimal set of image anchors and extensive textual descriptions, using frozen LLM semantic space to anchor evolving visual features.
AI.motivation: Deep learning models in medical imaging suffer catastrophic forgetting during continual adaptation. Existing incremental learning methods rely on rehearsing raw historical images, which incurs storage overhead, privacy risks, and fails to capture true data distributions with sparse exemplars.
AI.method: STAIL introduces (1) an asymmetric semantic consolidation buffer (SCB) that combines minimal image anchors with extensive text descriptions for dense semantic reconstruction at low storage cost, and (2) an LLM-derived Semantic Anchoring Mechanism (LSAM) that uses frozen LLM semantic space as developmental priors to anchor evolving visual features to textual representations at macroscopic and microscopic levels.
AI.result: Experiments across three heterogeneous medical datasets (fundus, ultrasound, X-ray) show STAIL acts as an effective plug-and-play module, improving existing baselines with average gains of 2.24% in AAA-AUC for sustained performance and 3.55% in BWT-AUC for reduced forgetting.
AI.conclusion: STAIL effectively addresses the rehearsal bottleneck in medical continual learning by leveraging semantic text anchoring, providing a privacy-preserving and storage-efficient alternative to raw image rehearsal while enhancing baseline performance across diverse imaging modalities.

title: Energy-Guided Flow Matching
summary: Pixel-space generative models bypass lossy latent compression, yet necessitate joint learning of global structure and fine-grained details in a high-dimensional space. Standard flow matching interpolates noise toward a fixed clean-image endpoint, leaving the spectral evolution to be learned implicitly. In this paper, we introduce Energy-Guided Flow Matching(EG-FM) that explicitly models a coarse-to-fine generative trajectory by moving endpoint. Specifically, EG-FM replaces the fixed endpoint with a heat-kernel-filtered endpoint that evolves smoothly from low-frequency image to clean image.The fraction of high-frequency signal in moving endpoint is released by an image-specific energy-guided scheduling, leading to the re-targeting of velocity in flow matching.Our framework requires no adaptation of the backbone and training data, bringing negligible cost on the training and inference stages. In our experiment, EG-FM consistently achieves lower FID on the ImageNet class-conditional image generation task at $256 \times 256$ with fewer epochs, reaching an FID of 1.55 at 200 epochs and 1.45 at 600 epochs. We continue training the generation task on the setting of $512 \times 512$ resolution, yielding a FID of 1.58 after only 40 high-resolution adaptation epochs.Furthermore, we transfer EG-FM on text-to-image generation and achieve 0.85 on GenEval score and 83.9 on DPG-Bench. Code is available at https://github.com/ysng123/EG-FM.

AI.tldr: EG-FM introduces Energy-Guided Flow Matching that replaces fixed clean-image endpoints with heat-kernel-filtered endpoints that evolve from low-frequency to clean images, explicitly modeling a coarse-to-fine generation trajectory with negligible extra cost.
AI.motivation: Pixel-space generative models must jointly learn global structure and fine details in high-dimensional space, but standard flow matching with fixed endpoints leaves spectral evolution to be learned implicitly rather than explicitly modeled.
AI.method: EG-FM replaces the fixed endpoint with a heat-kernel-filtered endpoint that smoothly evolves from low-frequency image to clean image. The fraction of high-frequency signal is released via image-specific energy-guided scheduling, which re-targets the velocity in flow matching. The framework requires no backbone or training data adaptation.
AI.result: Achieves FID of 1.55 at 200 epochs and 1.45 at 600 epochs on ImageNet 256x256 class-conditional generation; FID of 1.58 after only 40 high-resolution adaptation epochs at 512x512; 0.85 GenEval and 83.9 DPG-Bench on text-to-image generation.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly modeling the coarse-to-fine spectral trajectory through moving endpoints enables faster convergence and better generation quality across resolutions and task settings at negligible computational cost.

title: Bayesian adaptively-weighted ensembles for few-shot abdominal segmentation
comment: Accepted at DEMI at MICCAI 2026 - The 4th MICCAI Workshop in Data Engineering in Medical Imaging
summary: Few-shot learning has emerged as a promising approach for anatomical segmentation when labelled data are scarce. However, different few-shot learning algorithms exhibit complementary strengths and weaknesses, with performance varying across anatomical targets and institutions. Existing few-shot segmentation ensembles, that combine predictions from multiple algorithms, typically employ fixed weighting schemes and therefore cannot adjust model contributions according to the target domain. In this work, we propose a Bayesian adaptively-weighted ensemble framework for segmentation under label scarcity and domain shift. Multiple few-shot segmentation algorithms are first adapted using a small labelled support set. Bayesian optimisation is then used to automatically identify ensemble weights that maximise segmentation performance on a target-domain validation set. The learned weights are subsequently fixed and applied to combine predictions on previously unseen query images from the target domain. The proposed framework is evaluated on the Cross-institution Male Pelvic Structures dataset using held-out anatomical structures and institutions to simulate simultaneous label scarcity and institutional domain shift. Results demonstrate statistically significant improvements over individual few-shot learners, fixed-weight ensembles, training-from-scratch baselines and recent state-of-the-art ensembling approaches. By adapting model contributions to the target anatomy and institutional domain, the proposed framework provides a practical mechanism for deploying segmentation systems to new clinical sites under severe annotation constraints.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a Bayesian adaptively-weighted ensemble framework for few-shot segmentation that uses Bayesian optimization to automatically identify optimal ensemble weights on a target-domain validation set, improving segmentation performance under label scarcity and domain shift across anatomical targets and institutions.
AI.motivation: Different few-shot segmentation algorithms have complementary strengths and weaknesses that vary across anatomical targets and institutions. Existing ensemble methods use fixed weighting schemes and cannot adapt model contributions to the target domain, limiting their effectiveness.
AI.method: Multiple few-shot segmentation algorithms are first adapted using a small labelled support set. Bayesian optimization is then used to automatically discover ensemble weights that maximize segmentation performance on a target-domain validation set. The learned weights are fixed and applied to combine predictions on unseen query images from the target domain.
AI.result: Evaluated on the Cross-institution Male Pelvic Structures dataset with held-out anatomical structures and institutions. The framework demonstrates statistically significant improvements over individual few-shot learners, fixed-weight ensembles, training-from-scratch baselines, and recent state-of-the-art ensembling approaches.
AI.conclusion: By adapting model contributions to the target anatomy and institutional domain, the proposed framework provides a practical mechanism for deploying segmentation systems to new clinical sites under severe annotation constraints.

title: Controllable Clothing: Precise Labels and Generation for Virtual Try-On with Latent Diffusion Models
summary: In this technical report, I present a new method for guiding image generation in the context of Virtual- Try-On (VITON). The proposed method leverages new open source Ai models to augment the image data with labels, such as lengths and styles. By training adapters with these labels paired with images of the garments, the model can produce a more diverse set of images that the user can control. For the end user, such as a retailer, this means that they can assure that the produced image is as true to the true fit as possible, not misleading consumers

AI.tldr: This technical report presents a method for guiding image generation in Virtual Try-On (VITON) by augmenting image data with labels (e.g., lengths, styles) using open-source AI models, then training adapters with these labeled garment images to enable user-controlled, diverse image generation with accurate fit representation.
AI.motivation: The author aims to address the need for more controllable and accurate virtual try-on image generation, ensuring that generated images faithfully represent the true fit of garments to avoid misleading consumers in retail contexts.
AI.method: The method leverages new open-source AI models to augment image data with descriptive labels such as lengths and styles. These labels are paired with garment images, and adapters are trained on this labeled dataset to enable controlled and diverse image generation.
AI.result: The proposed approach produces a more diverse set of user-controllable images, allowing retailers to ensure the generated output reflects the true fit of the garment as accurately as possible.
AI.conclusion: This method provides end users, such as retailers, with a way to ensure that virtual try-on images are truthful to the actual fit, thereby avoiding consumer misinformation.

title: Accurate Localization of Road Traffic Objects on the Road Plane Using Surveillance Camera Imagery
comment: 8 pages, 7 figures. Accepted for publication in the proceedings of the 2026 Progress in Applied Electrical Engineering (PAEE) conference
summary:
Accurate vehicle localization from monocular roadside surveillance cameras is important for intelligent transportation systems, traffic monitoring, and traffic conflict analysis. Standard approaches often estimate vehicle position from the center of the detector bounding box, which can produce large errors due to perspective distortion and parallax, especially for elevated cameras and large vehicles.
  This paper proposes a two-stage geometry-aware localization pipeline that estimates the projection of the vehicle footprint onto the road plane. First, vehicles are detected using a YOLO26-based detector. Second, a dedicated ResNet34 regression network predicts four corner points corresponding to the projected vehicle base. The final position is computed as the geometric center of the predicted quadrilateral.
  The method was trained on synthetic data generated in CARLA and fine-tuned on real-world roadside imagery from DAIR-V2X. Experiments on synthetic and real data showed clear improvements over naive bounding-box-center localization. On DAIR-V2X, the mean image-space localization error decreased from 31.77 px to 15.30 px, a 51.8% improvement, while the median error decreased to 4.29 px. Median ground-plane error for medium-range vehicles decreased from 5.52 m to 0.90 m, and for far-range vehicles from 8.67 m to 1.84 m.
  The results also show that contextual information surrounding the detector bounding box is important for geometric localization. The largest gains were observed for distant vehicles and geometrically challenging cases affected by strong perspective distortion and parallax.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a two-stage geometry-aware pipeline for vehicle localization from monocular roadside cameras. It detects vehicles with YOLO26, then uses a ResNet34 network to predict the four corners of the vehicle's projected footprint on the road plane. The vehicle position is computed as the geometric center of the predicted quadrilateral. Trained on synthetic CARLA data and fine-tuned on DAIR-V2X real data, the method reduces mean image-space localization error from 31.77 px to 15.30 px (51.8% improvement) and median ground-plane error for medium-range vehicles from 5.52 m to 0.90 m.
AI.motivation: Standard vehicle localization approaches using bounding-box centers produce large errors due to perspective distortion and parallax, especially for elevated cameras and large vehicles. There is a need for more accurate vehicle positioning in intelligent transportation systems.
AI.method: A two-stage pipeline: (1) YOLO26-based detection of vehicles; (2) a dedicated ResNet34 regression network predicts four corner points corresponding to the projected vehicle base onto the road plane. The final position is the geometric center of the predicted quadrilateral. Training uses synthetic CARLA data, fine-tuned on real-world DAIR-V2X imagery.
AI.result: On DAIR-V2X, mean image-space localization error decreased from 31.77 px to 15.30 px (51.8% improvement), median error to 4.29 px. Median ground-plane error for medium-range vehicles decreased from 5.52 m to 0.90 m, and for far-range vehicles from 8.67 m to 1.84 m. Largest gains were for distant and geometrically challenging cases.
AI.conclusion: Predicting the projected vehicle footprint (quadrilateral) rather than relying on bounding-box centers significantly improves vehicle localization accuracy. Contextual information outside the bounding box is important for geometric localization, particularly for distant vehicles and cases with strong perspective distortion and parallax.

title: Overcoming Attention Drift: Homogeneity-Heterogeneity Guided Feature Aggregation for Low-Light Remote Sensing Image Enhancement
comment: 10 pages, 7 figures, 7 tables. Yaozi Zhong and Xingxing Yang contributed equally. Code: https://github.com/AlexYangxx/HALO
summary: Restoring high-fidelity remote sensing imagery from extreme low-light degradation is indispensable for reliable Earth observation and downstream machine vision. However, under severe noise and illumination corruption, existing methods suffer from attention drift, erroneously aggregating features across distinct physical boundaries and causing severe structural blurring and color distortion. To address this, we propose HALO, a dual-prior-driven enhancement framework that formulates enhancement as a guided feature aggregation problem driven by foundation model priors. Specifically, an illumination-invariant semantic prior provides regional homogeneity as a positive bias for content-consistent aggregation, while a pseudo-3D topological prior provides boundary heterogeneity as a negative penalty to strictly prevent cross-boundary confusion. To cooperatively incorporate these two priors, we propose a Homogeneity-Heterogeneity Cooperative Attention Module (H2CAM) to resolve feature conflicts during cross-modal prior fusion. Extensive experiments demonstrate that HALO achieves state-of-the-art performance across 8 challenging synthetic and real-world remote sensing benchmarks, significantly improving physical boundary sharpness and color fidelity while maximizing the preservation of discriminative features for downstream Earth observation tasks.

AI.tldr: HALO is a dual-prior-driven enhancement framework for restoring high-fidelity remote sensing imagery from extreme low-light degradation. It uses an illumination-invariant semantic prior for content-consistent aggregation and a pseudo-3D topological prior to prevent cross-boundary confusion, integrated via a Homogeneity-Heterogeneity Cooperative Attention Module (H2CAM), achieving state-of-the-art performance on 8 benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing low-light enhancement methods for remote sensing imagery suffer from attention drift under severe noise and illumination corruption, causing feature aggregation across distinct physical boundaries which leads to structural blurring and color distortion.
AI.method: Proposes HALO, a dual-prior-driven framework that formulates low-light enhancement as a guided feature aggregation problem. It leverages (1) an illumination-invariant semantic prior providing regional homogeneity as a positive bias, and (2) a pseudo-3D topological prior providing boundary heterogeneity as a negative penalty. A Homogeneity-Heterogeneity Cooperative Attention Module (H2CAM) resolves feature conflicts during cross-modal prior fusion.
AI.result: HALO achieves state-of-the-art performance across 8 challenging synthetic and real-world remote sensing benchmarks, significantly improving physical boundary sharpness and color fidelity while maximizing preservation of discriminative features for downstream Earth observation tasks.
AI.conclusion: The dual-prior-driven approach effectively addresses attention drift in extreme low-light remote sensing enhancement, improving both low-level image quality (boundary sharpness, color fidelity) and high-level downstream task performance.

title: Curia-MAE: Multi-Modal Multi-Anatomy MAE Pre-Training for 3D Medical Image Segmentation
summary: Radiology foundation models learn transferable representations that can be adapted to new tasks by training only small layers on top of a frozen encoder. Dense prediction tasks such as 3D segmentation are, however, underrepresented in their evaluation, and, with the encoder kept frozen, pre-trained models still fall short of nnU-Net, the state-of-the-art reference trained from scratch. To close this gap we extend convolutional MAE pre-training with a robust reconstruction objective, a feature regularizer, and a local-global similarity objective. Using this method, we propose Curia-MAE, a multi-modal, multi-anatomy MAE model pre-trained on 300,000 CT and MRI images covering a large number of anatomical sites. On eight anatomy- and lesion-focused segmentation benchmarks, Curia-MAE improves frozen-encoder performance over a strong MAE baseline, while remaining competitive under full finetuning and superior on lesion tasks, where labeled data is scarce. These results indicate that a single frozen encoder can be reused across diverse segmentation tasks, reducing the cost of adapting and deploying such models in clinical workflows. We will make our pre-trained model weights publicly available.

AI.tldr: Curia-MAE is a multi-modal, multi-anatomy radiology foundation model pre-trained on 300,000 CT and MRI images using convolutional MAE with a robust reconstruction objective, feature regularizer, and local-global similarity objective. It improves frozen-encoder segmentation performance over strong MAE baselines, remains competitive under full finetuning, and excels on lesion tasks with scarce labeled data.
AI.motivation: Radiology foundation models are typically evaluated on adaptation tasks, but dense prediction tasks like 3D segmentation are underrepresented. Pre-trained frozen encoders still fall short of nnU-Net (state-of-the-art trained from scratch), so there is a gap between foundation model transfer capabilities and specialized segmentation performance.
AI.method: Extends convolutional MAE pre-training with three components: (1) a robust reconstruction objective, (2) a feature regularizer, and (3) a local-global similarity objective. The model is pre-trained on 300,000 CT and MRI images covering a large number of anatomical sites.
AI.result: On eight anatomy- and lesion-focused segmentation benchmarks, Curia-MAE improves frozen-encoder performance over a strong MAE baseline, remains competitive under full finetuning, and shows superior performance on lesion tasks where labeled data is scarce.
AI.conclusion: A single frozen encoder from Curia-MAE can be reused across diverse segmentation tasks, reducing the cost of adapting and deploying radiology models in clinical workflows. Model weights will be made publicly available.

title: DTRNet: Dual Text-Radical Decoding for Handwritten Chinese Text Recognition with Faked Character Detection
summary: In K-12 educational scenarios, handwritten Chinese text recognition should not only transcribe student writing, but also detect faked characters. However, existing recognition models are usually confined to a predefined set of normal characters and therefore cannot explicitly identify faked characters. Existing detection methods exhibit complementary limitations: character-level methods provide interpretable structural evidence but suffer from low efficiency, whereas line-level methods are efficient but rely heavily on confidence scores, making them prone to missed detections and lacking explicit structural evidence. Thus, the key challenge is to preserve character-structural evidence independent of contextual inference while maintaining line-level efficiency. To this end, we propose DTRNet, a dual Text-Radical decoding framework for line-level faked character detection. DTRNet decouples context-aware text recognition from character-wise structural verification, where the text branch performs line-level transcription and the radical branch predicts legal Ideographic Description Sequences (IDS) for lexicon-based faked character judgment. We further introduce IDS-Guided Confidence Adjustment (IGCA) to refine text predictions using structural evidence during inference. Experimental results demonstrate that DTRNet effectively detects faked characters while maintaining strong recognition performance and providing interpretable radical-level evidence. Code, checkpoints, and the processed dataset are publicly available at https://github.com/BNU-ERC-ITEA/DTRNet.

AI.tldr: DTRNet is a dual text-radical decoding framework for line-level faked Chinese character detection in K-12 handwriting, decoupling context-aware recognition from character-wise structural verification via Ideographic Description Sequences (IDS) and IDS-Guided Confidence Adjustment (IGCA).
AI.motivation: Existing recognition models cannot explicitly identify faked characters because they are confined to predefined normal character sets. Detection methods have complementary limitations: character-level methods offer interpretable structural evidence but are inefficient, while line-level methods are efficient but rely on confidence scores, leading to missed detections and lacking explicit structural evidence. The key challenge is preserving character-structural evidence independent of contextual inference while maintaining line-level efficiency.
AI.method: DTRNet proposes a dual Text-Radical decoding framework that decouples context-aware text recognition (text branch) from character-wise structural verification (radical branch). The radical branch predicts legal Ideographic Description Sequences (IDS) for lexicon-based faked character judgment, and IDS-Guided Confidence Adjustment (IGCA) refines text predictions using structural evidence during inference.
AI.result: Experiments demonstrate that DTRNet effectively detects faked characters while maintaining strong recognition performance and providing interpretable radical-level evidence.
AI.conclusion: DTRNet successfully achieves line-level faked character detection with both strong recognition performance and interpretable structural evidence, with code and data publicly released.

title: Shape-Aware Oriented Bounding Box (OBB) to Horizontal Bounding Box (HBB) Conversion
summary: Accurate object detection in aerial and satellite imagery is dependent upon the bounding box representation. This is especially true for spatially oriented objects such as ships or aircrafts. Oriented Bounding Boxes (OBB) have a tighter fit and more robust non-max suppression compared to Horizontal Bounding Boxes (HBB), any current post-processing conversion from OBB to HBB either introduces excess empty and background space or removes data from the detection. This paper introduces a novel approach for a shape-aware OBB-to-HBB conversion for ship detection in remote sensing imagery. It leverages hull shape, hull fullness, and the bounding box orientation to produce a tighter axis-aligned HBB representation. The proposed method is benchmarked against three baselines methods for OBBto-HBB conversion, Outer HBB which uses minimum and maximum, Area Equivalent HBB and GBB Marginalized HBB.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a novel shape-aware method for converting Oriented Bounding Boxes (OBB) to Horizontal Bounding Boxes (HBB) specifically for ship detection in remote sensing imagery, using hull shape, hull fullness, and bounding box orientation to achieve tighter HBB representations compared to existing conversion methods.
AI.motivation: Existing OBB-to-HBB conversion methods either introduce excess empty/background space (tighter fit lost) or remove detection data, resulting in suboptimal bounding box representations for spatially oriented objects like ships in aerial and satellite imagery.
AI.method: The proposed method uses a shape-aware conversion approach that leverages three key features: hull shape, hull fullness, and bounding box orientation, to produce a tighter axis-aligned HBB representation during OBB-to-HBB conversion.
AI.result: The method is benchmarked against three baseline conversion methods: Outer HBB (minimum/maximum based), Area Equivalent HBB, and GBB Marginalized HBB, demonstrating improved tightness of the resulting bounding boxes.
AI.conclusion: A shape-aware OBB-to-HBB conversion approach can produce tighter HBBs for ship detection in remote sensing, overcoming the trade-off between excess background space and data loss found in prior conversion methods.

title: D-CLOT: Double Closed Loop Optimal Transport for Unsupervised Action Segmentation
summary: Optimal transport (OT) has emerged as an effective framework for unsupervised action segmentation. Yet, in existing OT-based methods, the latent action prototypes that define the OT costs are not re-estimated from the refined frame geometry. Instead, they evolve solely through gradients from the pseudo-label loss. We identify this \emph{representation--prototype inconsistency} as a central bottleneck, particularly around ambiguous transitions and for short or infrequent actions. To address this issue, we build on the recently introduced CLOT, which refines frame embeddings based on estimated segment embeddings, and further re-estimates the action prototypes from the refined frame embeddings. Specifically, we introduce a graph-constrained module that regularizes the OT-refined frame and segment representations by preserving the local neighborhood geometry of the encoder output. An action-embedding refinement step then periodically re-anchors the prototypes to this stabilized representation geometry. We study two instantiations that share the same backbone, graph module, and objective: D-CLOT updates the prototypes using $k$-means, whereas D-CLOT$_{B}$ updates them as OT barycenters weighted by the refined transport plan, yielding an assignment-aware prototype update consistent with the current transport geometry. Across five established benchmarks, both variants improve segment-level quality over CLOT, with per-video gains of up to $+12.7$ F1 and $+10.2$ mIoU (YTI) and activity-level gains of up to $+8.9$ F1 (FS-Eval). We further establish the first unsupervised action-segmentation baseline on Assembly101, a procedural and substantially more fine-grained benchmark than those commonly used in prior work. Extensive ablations and sensitivity analyses demonstrate that the two refinement mechanisms are complementary and robust.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces D-CLOT, an improvement over CLOT for unsupervised action segmentation, which addresses representation-prototype inconsistency by re-estimating action prototypes from OT-refined frame embeddings. Two instantiations (k-means and OT-barycenter based) achieve state-of-the-art results across five benchmarks with gains up to +12.7 F1.
AI.motivation: Existing OT-based action segmentation methods suffer from representation-prototype inconsistency: latent action prototypes defining OT costs are not re-estimated from refined frame geometry but evolve only through pseudo-label loss gradients. This is particularly problematic for ambiguous transitions, short actions, and infrequent actions.
AI.method: Builds on CLOT, which refines frame embeddings based on estimated segment embeddings, and adds: (1) a graph-constrained module that regularizes OT-refined frame and segment representations by preserving local neighborhood geometry of encoder output, and (2) an action-embedding refinement step that periodically re-anchors prototypes to the stabilized representation geometry. Two instantiations: D-CLOT uses k-means prototypes, D-CLOT_B uses OT barycenters weighted by the refined transport plan.
AI.result: Both variants improve segment-level quality over CLOT across five benchmarks, with per-video gains up to +12.7 F1 and +10.2 mIoU (YTI) and activity-level gains up to +8.9 F1 (FS-Eval). Also establishes the first unsupervised action-segmentation baseline on Assembly101, a more fine-grained benchmark.
AI.conclusion: The two refinement mechanisms (graph-constrained regularization and action-embedding refinement via k-means or OT-barycenters) are complementary and robust, as demonstrated by extensive ablations and sensitivity analyses.

title: MAVISEG: Manifold Propagation and Visual Prototypes for Zero-Shot Open-Vocabulary Segmentation in Diffusion Transformers
comment: 20 pages, 14 figures, 9 tables. Preprint under review
summary: Text-to-image diffusion transformers learn about objects and scenes by learning to generate them, making them strong candidates for training-free zero-shot open-vocabulary semantic segmentation. State-of-the-art attribution methods score each pixel independently, comparing its features against a fixed text-derived class representation, whether as an output-space similarity or as a cross-attention weight. This discards structured signals the model itself exposes: the temporal structure of the generative trajectory, the visual appearance statistics of each concept, and the image's own pairwise feature geometry. We present MAVISEG, a training-free refinement layer that recovers these signals. Because its operators consume only a pixel-by-concept score field and a pixel feature space, MAVISEG is capture-agnostic rather than tied to one attribution method. Across six benchmarks it achieves the strongest overall results among training-free methods, including the best mIoU on every benchmark. Interestingly, gains are largest where the initial capture is weakest, and individual operators contribute depending on the noise in the field they refine. Our results indicate that diffusion transformers carry more concept-level information than current attribution methods recover, and that much of it is lost on the way to the mask rather than absent from the model.

AI.tldr: MAVISEG is a training-free refinement layer that recovers structured signals (temporal generative trajectory, visual appearance statistics, and pairwise feature geometry) from text-to-image diffusion transformers for open-vocabulary semantic segmentation, achieving the strongest results among training-free methods across six benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing attribution methods score each pixel independently against fixed text-derived class representations, discarding structured signals the diffusion model itself exposes—temporal structure, visual appearance statistics, and pairwise feature geometry—which limits the quality of zero-shot semantic segmentation.
AI.method: MAVISEG is a training-free refinement layer that consumes only a pixel-by-concept score field and a pixel feature space, making it capture-agnostic (not tied to one attribution method). It recovers three structured signals: temporal structure of the generative trajectory, visual appearance statistics per concept, and the image's own pairwise feature geometry.
AI.result: Achieves the strongest overall results among training-free methods across six benchmarks, including the best mIoU on every benchmark. Gains are largest where the initial capture is weakest, and individual operators contribute depending on noise in the field they refine.
AI.conclusion: Diffusion transformers carry more concept-level information than current attribution methods recover, and much of it is lost on the way to the mask rather than absent from the model—meaning better signal recovery can unlock improved zero-shot segmentation without training.

title: To See a World in a Living Context: Unified Indoor-Outdoor Urban World Generation
summary: Text-driven 3D generation has advanced rapidly in creating large-scale outdoor environments and detailed indoor scenes, but these domains are usually synthesized independently, lacking the correspondence required for a coherent urban world. We present HoloWorld, a unified indoor-outdoor urban world generation framework built on a continuously updated cross-scale world context. Initializing from a user description, HoloWorld progressively represents and updates the diverse world information, from city-scale planning to individual buildings, allowing generated interiors to maintain explicit correspondence with their associated exterior buildings. Conditioned on the evolving context and previously generated neighboring blocks, HoloWorld autoregressively generates urban exteriors with consistent spatial organization and visual identity across blocks. The generated exterior representations are further grounded in 3D building instances and footprints, enabling building-specific indoor generation with geometry-constrained layouts and inherited appearance characteristics. To our knowledge, HoloWorld is the first framework to unify indoor and outdoor generation within a coherent 3D urban world. Extensive experiments demonstrate that HoloWorld achieves superior urban exterior generation performance, improving the average AQS score over the SOTA by 7.68\% and obtaining the highest average RDR score, while maintaining strong building-level indoor-outdoor correspondence and cross-block continuity within a unified 3D urban world.

AI.tldr: HoloWorld is a unified framework for generating coherent indoor-outdoor 3D urban worlds, maintaining explicit correspondence between indoor scenes and their associated exterior buildings through a continuously updated cross-scale world context.
AI.motivation: Existing text-driven 3D generation methods handle outdoor environments and indoor scenes independently, lacking the spatial and semantic correspondence required to create a coherent, unified urban world where interiors and exteriors are connected.
AI.method: HoloWorld builds on a continuously updated cross-scale world context that progresses from city-scale planning to individual buildings. It autoregressively generates urban exteriors conditioned on evolving context and neighboring blocks, grounding exterior representations in 3D building instances and footprints to enable building-specific indoor generation with geometry-constrained layouts and inherited appearance characteristics.
AI.result: HoloWorld improves the average AQS score over the state-of-the-art by 7.68% and achieves the highest average RDR score, while maintaining strong building-level indoor-outdoor correspondence and cross-block continuity.
AI.conclusion: HoloWorld is the first framework to unify indoor and outdoor generation within a coherent 3D urban world, demonstrating superior performance in urban exterior generation and cross-scale consistency.

title: Robust-WAM: Bridging Generative Pretraining and Semantic Foresight in World-Action Models
summary: Mainstream World-Action Models (WAMs) adapt pretrained video generation models (VGMs) for robot control, transferring their learned dynamics prior for action prediction. These VGMs are typically trained in a variational autoencoder (VAE) latent space. However, the VAE latent space is optimized for pixel reconstruction, which rewards fine appearance detail and leaves the action prediction fragile under visual shifts. Recent works build WAMs in semantic latent space, which are more robust to appearance shifts. However, these models cannot leverage the large-scale VGM pretraining that exists only in VAE space. To overcome this dilemma, we propose Robust-WAM, a general post-training method for video-generation-based WAMs that preserves the VAE-based generative path and adds a lightweight semantic foresight alignment objective on the action stream. This retains the large-scale VGM pretraining while grounding actions in appearance-invariant dynamics that stay reliable under illumination shifts and other visual out-of-distribution conditions. Specifically, we employ learnable query tokens to bring future-scene semantics into the action stream by aligning their output hidden states with the semantic foresight of future ground-truth frames. To establish the temporal correspondence between each query and the future step it describes, we give it the positional encoding of the matching action tokens. Experiments on out-of-distribution generalization simulation benchmarks and a real-robot setup show that our Robust-WAM consistently improves the success rates of multiple WAM baselines without sacrificing in-distribution performance.

AI.tldr: Robust-WAM is a post-training method for World-Action Models that adds a lightweight semantic foresight alignment objective to the action stream while preserving VAE-based generative pretraining, improving robustness to visual shifts in robot control without sacrificing in-distribution performance.
AI.motivation: World-Action Models built on VAE latent spaces inherit a representation optimized for pixel reconstruction, which makes action prediction fragile under visual shifts (e.g., illumination changes). While semantic latent spaces offer better robustness, they cannot leverage the large-scale VGM pretraining that exists only in VAE space. This creates a dilemma between leveraging powerful pretraining and achieving robust action prediction.
AI.method: Robust-WAM preserves the existing VAE-based generative path and adds a lightweight semantic foresight alignment objective on the action stream. Learnable query tokens are used to bring future-scene semantics into the action stream by aligning their hidden states with semantic foresight of future ground-truth frames. Each query receives the positional encoding of its corresponding action token to establish temporal correspondence.
AI.result: Experiments on out-of-distribution generalization simulation benchmarks and a real-robot setup show consistent improvements in success rates across multiple WAM baselines, without sacrificing in-distribution performance.
AI.conclusion: Robust-WAM effectively bridges the gap between VAE-space VGM pretraining and semantic robustness by grounding actions in appearance-invariant dynamics, demonstrating that semantic alignment on the action stream is a general and effective post-training strategy for video-generation-based WAMs.

title: Mapping Armenian Paris: Extracting and Geocoding Commercial Advertisements from the 20th-Century Diaspora Press
summary: This paper presents an end-to-end, IIIF-based pipeline that turns the digitised Armenian press of France into an interactive map of the 20th-century Parisian Armenian commercial community. On each page, commercial advertisements are located, read, and parsed into structured records, which are then geocoded and placed on the map. Western Armenian is under-resourced and unsupported by off-the-shelf layout and OCR models, so the pipeline uses vision-language models (VLMs) as a data-bootstrapping strategy: they produce usable structured records at a scale hand annotation could not reach, and stay reliable on the strongly curved scans where conventional line-level CRNN OCR breaks down. The contribution includes a 500-page Western Armenian press corpus with 3,270 advertisement-level annotations, a Label Studio template that captures detection and semantic fields in a single annotation pass, and a reproducible workflow transposable to other under-resourced historical corpora. More broadly, the work shows that VLM-driven data bootstrapping is an effective lever for under-resourced historical languages such as (Western) Armenian.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an end-to-end IIIF-based pipeline that converts digitised French Armenian press into an interactive map of 20th-century Parisian Armenian commerce. It uses vision-language models (VLMs) to locate, read, and parse commercial advertisements on each page, then geocodes them onto a map, demonstrating VLM-driven data bootstrapping as an effective strategy for under-resourced historical languages like Western Armenian.
AI.motivation: Western Armenian is under-resourced and unsupported by off-the-shelf layout and OCR models, and conventional line-level CRNN OCR breaks down on strongly curved scans, making hand annotation infeasible at scale. The authors aim to make this historical corpus accessible through an interactive geographic interface.
AI.method: The pipeline is end-to-end and IIIF-based: commercial advertisements are located, read, and parsed into structured records on each page using vision-language models (VLMs) as a data-bootstrapping strategy. A Label Studio template captures detection and semantic fields in a single annotation pass.
AI.result: The pipeline produced a 500-page Western Armenian press corpus with 3,270 advertisement-level annotations. VLMs produced usable structured records at a scale hand annotation could not reach and remained reliable on strongly curved scans where conventional CRNN OCR fails.
AI.conclusion: VLM-driven data bootstrapping is an effective lever for under-resourced historical languages such as Western Armenian, and the reproducible workflow is transposable to other under-resourced historical corpora.

title: Floating Radiance Networks
summary: Recent advances in neural scene representations enable photorealistic novel-view synthesis, yet most methods remain tightly coupled to a single rendering paradigm, limiting their versatility and integration with conventional graphics workflows. We introduce Floating Radiance Networks (FlaRe), a neural scene representation combining explicit ray-traceable geometry with continuous neural radiance functions. A scene is represented by floating planar generalized Gaussian primitives, each carrying a compact latent descriptor of a local radiance field. A lightweight decoder shared across the scene maps this descriptor, local surface coordinates, and viewing direction to color and opacity. This formulation preserves the expressiveness of neural fields while providing an explicitly addressable structure that can be efficiently queried and manipulated. Hardware-accelerated primitive intersections enable interactive rendering and recursive ray-tracing, including reflections, refractions, transparency, and shadows. The same representation further supports primitive-level deformation, mesh extraction, and appearance stylization directly in its learned descriptor space. Experiments across standard reconstruction benchmarks demonstrate competitive rendering quality while using a compact set of primitives. Together, these results establish FlaRe as a versatile representation that brings high-fidelity neural rendering, ray-tracing, geometric manipulation, and appearance editing into a unified scene model. Source code is available online. Source code can be found at: https://github.com/KByrski/FlaRe

AI.tldr: FlaRe is a neural scene representation using floating planar Gaussian primitives with latent descriptors and a shared lightweight decoder, enabling ray-tracing, interactive rendering, geometric manipulation, and appearance editing in a unified model.
AI.motivation: Most neural scene representations are tied to a single rendering paradigm, limiting their integration with conventional graphics workflows such as ray-tracing, mesh extraction, and manipulation.
AI.method: Scene is represented by floating planar generalized Gaussian primitives, each carrying a compact latent descriptor of a local radiance field. A shared lightweight decoder maps descriptors, local surface coordinates, and viewing direction to color and opacity. Hardware-accelerated primitive intersections enable interactive rendering and recursive ray-tracing.
AI.result: Competitive rendering quality on standard reconstruction benchmarks while using a compact set of primitives, while supporting ray-tracing effects (reflections, refractions, transparency, shadows), deformation, mesh extraction, and stylization.
AI.conclusion: FlaRe establishes a versatile unified scene model that bridges high-fidelity neural rendering with traditional graphics capabilities including ray-tracing, geometric manipulation, and appearance editing.

title: MirrorNet: Can Medical Image Anonymization Really Protect Patient Identity?
summary: Medical images are routinely de-identified---names, dates, and other metadata removed---and then shared for research, teaching, and public benchmarks under the assumption that this renders them anonymous.
